stories.s: Messenger now lets users filter conversations by status, cutting the time attendees and exhibitors spend hunting through a cluttered inbox to find active or pending threads.
stories.pr: The Messenger inbox presented all conversations as one undifferentiated list, so users could not quickly isolate open, pending or closed threads during a busy event.
stories.oc: Conversation status filters were added to Messenger so users can narrow the thread list by state.

stories.s: A scroll hint was added to the time picker so users immediately realise more time slots are available below the fold, reducing missed selections when booking meetings.
stories.pr: Users did not realise the time picker was scrollable, so available slots below the visible area went unnoticed and booking friction increased.
stories.oc: A visual scroll hint cue was introduced on the time picker control.

stories.s: Exhibitor events now appear in a sensible order within the exhibitor profile, so attendees can scan an exhibitor's sessions in a predictable sequence instead of a random list.
stories.pr: Exhibitor events listed on the exhibitor profile lacked a defined sort order, making the list hard to scan and undermining trust in the profile presentation.
stories.oc: Deterministic sorting was applied to the exhibitor-events list inside the exhibitor profile.

stories.s: Lead capture in the mobile booth now autosaves the moment an exhibitor leaves the form, guaranteeing no scanned lead or partial data is ever lost even on flaky venue networks.
stories.pr: Exhibitors risked losing captured lead data if they navigated away or the app/network dropped before manually saving, costing them valuable booth leads.
stories.oc: Lead data now autosaves on exit, back action, app close, or network loss (queued locally and synced), creating or updating a lead and recording engagement.

stories.s: MTT's infrastructure-as-code was rebuilt to match Recommendation Service standards, making the AI service safer to deploy toward production.
stories.pr: MTT's infrastructure was POC-grade and inconsistent with the team's established IaC best practices, raising deployment and maintenance risk.
stories.oc: MTT infrastructure-as-code was refactored to follow Recommendation Service best practices.

stories.s: Meetings export was migrated to the V3 public API with rich filtering and incremental sync, letting integration partners pull meeting data reliably and at scale.
stories.pr: Meeting data export lacked a modern, filterable V3 API endpoint, limiting partners' ability to retrieve and incrementally sync meeting data.
stories.oc: Delivered GET /api/v3/meetings with pagination, time/created/modified filters, account filtering and timestamp-based incremental fetch returning ISO8601 data.

stories.s: Saving or applying changes across key Admin Panel modules no longer kicks organizers off the page, removing constant rework and navigation loss while they configure an event.
stories.pr: In several Admin Panel modules, Save/Apply redirected users away from the current page, causing repeated navigation, rework and disrupted configuration workflows.
stories.oc: Backend support so Save/Apply preserves the current view in Exhibitor Manual-Vendors, Marketing (News, Slugs, Campaigns) and the Mobile app builder.

stories.s: Organizers can now clone Product Category custom filters within an event, eliminating the manual rebuild of complex filter sets every time a new event is created or cloned.
stories.pr: Custom filters for Product Categories had to be reconfigured by hand for every new or cloned event, a slow and error-prone setup task.
stories.oc: Backend capability to clone Product Category custom filters within an event during the pre-event phase.

stories.s: Selecting a parent category in Networking now auto-selects all its child categories, turning a tedious one-by-one click chore into a single action during event matchmaking setup.
stories.pr: Organizers had to manually select each child category individually because parent selection did not cascade, slowing the matchmaking setup workflow.
stories.oc: Added a Select All checkbox that recursively selects a parent and all descendant categories, with the ability to deselect individuals and auto-deselect children when the parent is unchecked.

stories.s: Integrations can now assign HYVE-matched contacts as admins automatically, without downgrading existing admin roles on every resync.
stories.pr: Integration always created team members as 'member' and resync overwrote roles, so admins assigned to exhibitors were silently demoted and HYVE's contact-person-as-admin rule could not be honoured.
stories.oc: Role can be defined via integration settings/mapping; HYVE rule sets admin when member email matches the exhibitor contact; existing roles are preserved on resync when not explicitly mapped.

stories.s: Mobile Favorites is being reworked with hall/booth filtering and sorting, aligning it with Web for easier on-site exhibitor planning.
stories.pr: On mobile, attendees could not filter or sort favorited exhibitors/products by hall or booth, and a redundant Favorite Products tab created an inconsistent, disconnected experience versus Web.
stories.oc: Consolidating Favorites into one page with All/Mutual/Exhibitor/Visitor/Product/Speaker tabs and richer filter/sort options aligned to Web (in progress).

stories.s: A backend API was implemented for the new Recommendation Service, giving the platform a clean integration point to surface category-based recommendations to participants.
stories.pr: The recreated Recommendation Service needed a defined backend API so the platform could consume its category-based recommendations.
stories.oc: Implemented the recommendation service API per the documented backend integration contract.

stories.s: AI meeting-notes now sends one shared action-point list to all participants instead of per-person lists, eliminating a defect where misattributed speakers sent people the wrong action items.
stories.pr: MTT generated a separate action-point list per participant, but speaker misrecognition sometimes sent attendees the wrong action points, undermining trust in the AI notes.
stories.oc: Action points are combined into a single list sent identically to every participant, with speaker-name prefixes and a 2-6 item range.

stories.s: The final tranche of work for the MYS native integration was delivered, closing out the remaining gaps so the MYS client's end-to-end integration needs are fully met.
stories.pr: The MYS native integration still had outstanding tasks that left parts of the client's data-sync needs uncovered.
stories.oc: Completed the remaining MYS integration tasks (stage 2) covering the outstanding user needs.

stories.s: Robust filters were added to the admin Sessions and Exhibitor Events pages, mirroring the Exhibitor Directory so organizers stop scrolling through flat lists to find specific sessions or events.
stories.pr: The Sessions and Exhibitor Events admin pages were flat lists with little filtering, forcing organizers to manually scan to locate items unlike the well-filtered Exhibitor Directory.
stories.oc: Added independent filter sections (e.g. session type and more) to both the Sessions page and the Exhibitor Events page.

stories.s: Custom badge errors in the Aditus integration now route users to a clear, localized error page (with German) instead of silently reverting to the native badge, so attendees know what action to take.
stories.pr: When a custom badge could not be retrieved, the app showed an error then reverted to the native badge page, a poor experience that left users without guidance.
stories.oc: Users are redirected to appropriate error pages with refined English copy and added German variants for no-connection and no-information cases.

stories.s: A toggle now lets organizers fully disable notifications for a specific Meeting Program on Web and App, delivered as an urgent hotfix to meet a HYVE requirement to suppress unwanted meeting alerts.
stories.pr: There was no way to stop notifications for a particular Meeting Program, and HYVE urgently needed to prevent these alerts from being sent.
stories.oc: Added a 'Disable notifications' ON/OFF toggle (default OFF) on Meeting Program create/edit settings that suppresses all related Web and App notifications when enabled.

stories.s: The mobile Sessions list now auto-scrolls to and highlights what's happening now and next, sparing attendees with large agendas from endless scrolling to find current sessions.
stories.pr: The mobile Sessions list always opened at the start of the day, so attendees with large agendas had to scroll extensively to reach sessions happening now, with no one-tap jump to 'now'.
stories.oc: Auto-scroll to the current time with a now separator and Now/Upcoming highlighting that applies only when the selected day is today (server-confirmed).

stories.s: The Meeting Program report's All Meetings tab gained a column showing how each meeting was generated, giving organizers visibility into meeting source for better reporting and analysis.
stories.pr: The All Meetings report did not expose how meetings were generated, so organizers lacked insight into meeting source when analysing program performance.
stories.oc: Added an extra column on the All Meetings tab indicating each meeting's generation source.

stories.s: A new AI search service was built and deployed, letting participants semantically search exhibitor profiles, team members, and products.
stories.pr: The platform lacked a deployed AI/semantic search capability for participants to find exhibitors, team members and products, and needed a technology decision (vector DB vs search engine).
stories.oc: Built and deployed an AI search service (exposed via API) covering exhibitor profiles, team-member profiles, and products/sessions, after evaluating PGVector vs Typesense alternatives.

stories.s: Speed Networking can now exchange large input/output JSON via S3 through dedicated API endpoints, removing payload-size limits on scaling.
stories.pr: Passing Speed Networking input/output directly was unsuitable for large datasets, constraining scalability and reliability of the calculation flow.
stories.oc: Added three API endpoints to request an S3 location for input, trigger the Speed Networking calculation, and poll status/retrieve the output location, including in-progress responses.

stories.s: Mobile exhibitor search now ranks name matches above description matches, so attendees typing an exhibitor name see the right result at the top instead of scrolling past unrelated hits.
stories.pr: Mobile search matched on both exhibitor name and description, so the expected exhibitor often did not appear at the top, forcing users to scroll through irrelevant results.
stories.oc: Search results are now ordered to prioritise exhibitor-name matches (exact name first) ahead of description matches.

stories.s: The CDS participant integration now supports paginated pulls with full field mapping and admin-configurable parameters, enabling reliable large-volume registration sync for the client.
stories.pr: The CDS participant registration integration needed paginated retrieval and configurable mapping to import large registrant datasets reliably into participant categories and profiles.
stories.oc: Implemented paginated participant import mapping reg fields to participant data, email-based update matching, and admin-panel settings for OrderType and IncludeItems.

stories.s: Login now offers two clear paths, SAML SSO for buyers and standard EP login for API-created team members, so both can authenticate.
stories.pr: With SAML enabled, API-created team members who must use the standard EP login had no clean path, creating an authentication conflict between SSO buyers and credential-based members.
stories.oc: A sign-in modal now offers two options: SAML redirect to the identity provider, or the standard EP login flow.

stories.s: Meeting Program gained sorting options for its Relevance and Opt-in phases, letting organizers order participants meaningfully during matchmaking instead of working from an unsorted list.
stories.pr: The Meeting Program Relevance and opt-in phases lacked sorting controls, making it harder for organizers to prioritise and review participants during matchmaking.
stories.oc: Added sorting options for the Relevance and opt-in phases of the Meeting Program.

stories.s: Surfacing meeting ratings inside the organizer's All Meetings tab gives event teams an at-a-glance read on meeting quality across the whole programme.
stories.pr: Meeting ratings collected after sessions were not visible in the consolidated All Meetings view, so organizers had no easy way to gauge how well meetings were received.
stories.oc: The All Meetings tab of the Meeting Program report now displays the rating each meeting received, making quality measurable in one place.

stories.s: A persistent, non-blocking banner now warns admins not to edit an event while it is being cloned, eliminating a recurring source of data corruption.
stories.pr: Event cloning gave no visible signal in the Admin Panel, so organizers edited source events mid-clone and repeatedly produced inconsistent, broken event setups.
stories.oc: A fixed informational banner is shown across all Admin Panel module pages of the source event while cloning runs, telling users not to make changes until it completes.

stories.s: UI improvements to the exhibitor-profile Custom Questions page make it easier for exhibitors and organizers to work through custom data capture as part of Lead Intelligence.
stories.pr: The Custom Questions page in the exhibitor profile had usability friction that made configuring and answering custom questions harder than it needed to be.
stories.oc: The Custom Questions page received UI refinements to improve clarity and ease of use within the exhibitor profile.

stories.s: Showing general buyers during the relevance stage of the Meeting Program widens the pool of potential matches exhibitors can see and engage during matchmaking.
stories.pr: During the relevance stage, general (non-targeted) buyers were not surfaced, limiting the matchmaking opportunities visible to exhibitors.
stories.oc: The Meeting Program now displays general buyers during the relevance stage, expanding who exhibitors can be matched with.

stories.s: Automatically removing deleted users from the Meeting Program keeps the matchmaking and scheduling data clean so meetings are not booked against accounts that no longer exist.
stories.pr: When users were deleted, they remained referenced in the Meeting Program, leaving stale participants that could break scheduling and matchmaking integrity.
stories.oc: Deleted users are now stripped from the Meeting Program, so only valid participants appear in matchmaking and meeting data.

stories.s: Planning the ClickHouse version upgrade de-risks the analytics datastore by scoping the migration before execution, protecting reporting reliability as data volumes grow.
stories.pr: The ClickHouse (CH) database was on a version that needed upgrading, but the upgrade path and risks had not yet been planned, leaving the analytics backend exposed.
stories.oc: A plan for the ClickHouse version upgrade was produced by the Data Science team, defining the approach for the actual upgrade.

stories.s: Giving organizers a manual delete-meetings control in the Meeting Program lets them clean up incorrect or cancelled meetings directly, without engineering intervention.
stories.pr: Organizers could not manually remove meetings from the Meeting Program, so erroneous or cancelled meetings lingered and required workarounds.
stories.oc: A manual delete-meetings capability was added to the Meeting Program, with confirmation and schedule views defined in the linked designs.

stories.s: An admin-side No Show capability lets organizers mark meeting no-shows, improving the accuracy of meeting attendance and reporting in the Meeting Program.
stories.pr: Organizers had no way to record that a participant failed to attend a scheduled meeting, leaving attendance data incomplete.
stories.oc: The Meeting Program admin gained a No Show control (with confirmation/schedule views per the linked designs) to flag missed meetings.

stories.s: The user-facing side of No Show lets meeting participants themselves register a counterpart's no-show, feeding attendance accuracy from both sides of each meeting.
stories.pr: Participants had no way to report when the other party did not turn up to a scheduled meeting, so no-shows went unrecorded from the user side.
stories.oc: A user-facing No Show capability was delivered so meeting participants can flag no-shows themselves, complementing the admin control.

stories.s: Removing deleted users from Round Tables sessions keeps networking session rosters clean so deleted accounts no longer occupy seats or distort session data.
stories.pr: Deleted users stayed attached to Round Tables sessions, leaving phantom participants that consumed capacity and corrupted session integrity.
stories.oc: Deleted users are now removed from Round Tables sessions, so only valid participants remain on session rosters.

stories.s: A standing time-tracking practice has the team log synchronous meeting time monthly, giving leadership visibility into meeting overhead across the team.
stories.pr: There was no measurement of how much time the team spent in meetings and calls, so meeting overhead was invisible to management.
stories.oc: A monthly per-person meeting-time logging convention was set up (one sub-task per person per month) to capture synchronous meeting/call time; work is ongoing.

stories.s: Showing each participant's profile-completion status in the admin Participants list lets organizers spot incomplete profiles at a glance and chase richer attendee data.
stories.pr: Organizers could not see how complete each participant's profile was from the Participants list, making it hard to identify and improve sparse profiles.
stories.oc: The admin-panel Participants list now displays profile completion for each participant.

stories.s: Reworking the mobile global force-resync so it no longer logs users out lets organizers fully reset event data mid-event (delivered for Shoptalk) without disrupting attendees.
stories.pr: The admin-panel global resync logged all users out during a full database reset/resync, disrupting attendees during live events.
stories.oc: The admin-panel global resync was modified to perform a full reset/resync without logging users out, matching the in-app settings resync functionality.

stories.s: Making the Meeting Transcription Tool produce outputs in the meeting's own language fixes a multilingual usability gap that undermined the AI meeting artifacts.
stories.pr: MTT (AI meeting notes) outputs did not consistently match the language of the conversation, making artifacts less useful for multilingual users.
stories.oc: MTT now generates its outputs in the language of the meeting, so transcripts/notes match the conversation language.

stories.s: Updating how participant profile completion is calculated gives organizers and attendees a more accurate completeness score that drives profile-quality nudges.
stories.pr: The existing profile-completion calculation did not accurately reflect how complete a participant's profile was, undermining trust in the metric.
stories.oc: The participant profile-completion calculation logic was updated to produce a more accurate completion value.

stories.s: Adding a profile-completion column to participant export reports lets organizers analyse and act on profile quality outside the platform, in their own reporting flows.
stories.pr: Participant export reports did not include profile-completion data, so organizers could not analyse completeness in exported spreadsheets.
stories.oc: Exported participant reports now include a Profile Completion column.

stories.s: Letting organizers upload one Exhibitor Manual document with a separate file per event language replaces the messy multi-entry workaround and is the admin-side half of proper multilingual manuals.
stories.pr: Exhibitor Manual documents had no language-level association, so organizers created separate entries per language and all variants showed at once regardless of the selected event language, confusing exhibitors.
stories.oc: Organizers can now upload language-specific files for each enabled event language within a single Exhibitor Manual entry (admin-side; the frontend half is EP-49298).

stories.s: On the exhibitor-facing side, exhibitors now see only the Exhibitor Manual file matching their selected event language, completing the multilingual manual experience.
stories.pr: In Online Exhibitor Services, all language variants of a manual displayed simultaneously regardless of the chosen event language, so exhibitors saw multiple versions with no guarantee of a language match.
stories.oc: Online Exhibitor Services now serves each exhibitor the Exhibitor Manual document in their selected event language only.

stories.s: Adding a configurable second external login button to the mobile app lets a client offer attendees an alternate webview-based sign-in path, satisfying a specific customer requirement.
stories.pr: The native mobile login screen supported only a single login option, but a client needed a second, externally-hosted login route surfaced to their users.
stories.oc: A second external login button was added to the native login screen (type 'Both'), opening the existing webview login flow with configurable label/colour, plus new App Builder/API settings to control it.

stories.s: Aligning the new recommendation service's entities and output exactly with the legacy service de-risks the cutover, ensuring matchmaking quality doesn't regress when the rebuild ships.
stories.pr: The new recommendation service was built from the current service's code and risked having overlooked entities, so its output might not match the proven current recommender.
stories.oc: Recommendation entities in the new service were aligned with the current service and verified so the new recommender's output matches the existing one.

stories.s: Organizers of co-located events can now compare check-ins across events and see crossover check-ins in the Check-In/Check-Out graph.
stories.pr: Check-in analytics treated each event in isolation, so organizers running co-located events could not compare attendance or see attendees who crossed between events by badge origin.
stories.oc: The Total Check-In / Check-Out graph now supports comparing check-ins across co-located events and surfaces crossover check-ins, filterable by badge origin.

stories.s: Cutting the recommendation service's cold-start time (previously 30-50s on a tenant's first request) sharply improves responsiveness of matchmaking for the first user of each event.
stories.pr: The recommendation service's inference cache loaded tenant/event data from the database on first access, making the first request for a tenant take roughly 30-50 seconds.
stories.oc: The recommendation inference cold-start path was optimised to significantly reduce first-request response time without affecting recommendation accuracy.

stories.s: Personalized Meeting Notes (Core) on web delivers tailored AI meeting-note output to each user, deepening the platform's AI meeting-intelligence offering.
stories.pr: Not Clearly Specified — description is a Confluence link; the title indicates meeting notes were not yet personalized per user on web.
stories.oc: The core of Personalized Meeting Notes was delivered on web, providing user-tailored meeting notes.

stories.s: Letting organizers control AI Notetaker access by exhibitor category gives them governance over who can use the AI meeting-notes feature, supporting tiered or paid access models.
stories.pr: Not Clearly Specified in body (Confluence link); the title shows there was no way to gate AI Notetaker access by exhibitor category.
stories.oc: Admins gained controls to enable or restrict AI Notetaker access based on exhibitor category.

stories.s: Per-exhibitor and per-category control over AI Notes gives organizers fine-grained governance of the AI notes feature down to individual exhibitors, extending the category-level access control.
stories.pr: Not Clearly Specified in body (Confluence link); the title indicates AI Notes lacked per-exhibitor / per-category granularity of control.
stories.oc: Admins can now control AI Notes access at both per-exhibitor and per-category level.

stories.s: Organizers can now switch on and price AI Meeting Notes as a paid Lead Capture Pro add-on, turning the transcription tool into a new monetisable upsell to sell to exhibitors.
stories.pr: AI Meeting Notes existed as a capability but had no commercial packaging, so organizers had no way to sell it or capture revenue from it within Lead Capture Pro.
stories.oc: Admin Panel Lead Capture Pro now has an AI Meeting Notes add-on card with an enable/disable toggle and a configurable price that auto-matches the event payment currency.

stories.s: Reworked AI exhibitor search so exact partner name matches outrank coordinators that merely mention the term in their description, ensuring buyers at IMEX land on the right company.
stories.pr: Coordinators whose descriptions contained look-alike words (e.g. 'according' for a search of 'Accor') were outranking the actual partner the buyer wanted, producing irrelevant top results.
stories.oc: Introduced hybrid name-priority scoring on top of semantic search so name-field matches always score above description-level hits across exhibitor entities.

stories.s: Built a lightweight branded search front-end so the AI search pilot could be demonstrated to IMEX stakeholders without raw API calls.
stories.pr: Pilot search behaviour could only be shown via manual calls in the Qdrant UI, which was not presentable to a non-technical audience.
stories.oc: Delivered a polished demo UI with a search box and typeahead autocomplete that calls the search and /autocomplete endpoints and groups results by entity type.

stories.s: Routed partial-name typeahead through a dedicated fast autocomplete endpoint so over-lenient substring matching no longer floods AI search with noise.
stories.pr: Lenient substring matching dragged in unrelated results (e.g. 'acc' pulling in 'ACC - Air Charter' for 'Accor'), degrading search precision.
stories.oc: Added a separate prefix-indexed /autocomplete endpoint (~50ms) that keeps noisy substring behaviour out of full search and surfaces clean name suggestions.

stories.s: Made AI search resilient to spacing and special-character differences so a query like 'Visit Scotland' still finds 'VisitScotland'.
stories.pr: Spaces and special characters broke name matches - exhibitors registered without spaces did not surface when users typed the spaced form (and vice versa), a confirmed pilot blocker.
stories.oc: Tokeniser handling was fixed so spaced and unspaced/concatenated brand-name variants resolve to the correct exhibitor in top results.

stories.s: Added cultural-name and diacritic tolerance to AI search so endonym/exonym variants (e.g. 'Italia' for 'Italy') return the right exhibitors.
stories.pr: Searches using native-language or cultural name variants hit dead ends because multilingual endonym-exonym variants and accented characters were not recognised.
stories.oc: Combined semantic similarity with ascii_folding character normalisation so common language variants and diacritic differences surface relevant results instead of zero results.

stories.s: Encoded the coordinator/partner hierarchy into AI search so exhibitor results follow a consistent parent/child ranking order.
stories.pr: The coordinator/partner (parent/child) relationship was absent from the search data model, so exhibitor results could not be ranked in the intended four-tier order.
stories.oc: Extracted the parent/child relationship from PostgreSQL into the Qdrant payload during ingestion, enabling coordinator-exact, partner-exact, coordinator-fuzzy, partner-fuzzy ordering.

stories.s: Extended AI search coverage by indexing People, Sessions, Products and News so name matches across all entity types rank correctly.
stories.pr: Only some entities were indexed, so exact person/session/product/news name matches could be outranked by similarly named companies or not appear at all.
stories.oc: Indexed the People, News, Product and Session entities in Qdrant so exact name matches surface and rank above weaker description-level matches, consistent with other entity types.

stories.s: Replaced empty AI-search dead-ends with helpful 'Did you mean...?' and category fallback prompts so buyers always have a next step.
stories.pr: Weak or zero-result searches showed blank dead-end pages instead of suggestions or nearby category prompts.
stories.oc: Added fallback handling so a no-results query surfaces a no-results message with 'Did you mean...?' suggestions and category prompts rather than an empty page.

stories.pr: The /api/v2/sessions/removeSession endpoint lacked dedicated QA, so destructive delete behaviour was untested for external integrators.
stories.oc: The removeSession endpoint was exercised against a defined scope and any defects were logged as separate linked bugs, confirming safe deletion behaviour.

stories.s: QA validation of the V2 Open API sessions getOnlineExport endpoint, ensuring exported session data is correct for partners relying on the public API.
stories.pr: The /api/v2/sessions/getOnlineExport endpoint had no dedicated QA coverage, leaving its export output unverified for external consumers.
stories.oc: The getOnlineExport endpoint was tested to a defined scope with defects captured as individual linked bugs, validating the export path.

stories.s: QA validation of the V2 Open API sessions/set write endpoint, reducing the risk of corrupt session writes reaching partner integrations.
stories.pr: The /api/v2/sessions/set endpoint lacked structured QA, so its create/update write behaviour was unverified on the public API.
stories.oc: The sessions/set endpoint was exercised against a defined scope and defects logged as individual linked bugs, validating the write path.

stories.s: Meeting ratings now surface in the mobile app as soon as attendees receive their final schedule, capturing feedback earlier in the meeting-program lifecycle.
stories.pr: Meeting ratings only appeared after a Meeting Program ended, so attendees could not rate individual meetings while the program was still running and feedback was lost.
stories.oc: Ratings become available for each meeting at the moment it appears in the app via the Final Schedule, rather than only after the program concludes.

stories.s: Exhibitors can now buy AI Meeting Notes directly on the Lead Capture Pro page, instantly unlocking AI transcription for their whole team.
stories.pr: Even once the add-on could be priced by organizers, exhibitors had no front-end surface to purchase AI Meeting Notes, leaving the monetisation path incomplete with no way to capture revenue.
stories.oc: The Lead Capture Pro purchasing page shows a buyable AI Meeting Notes option when enabled, flips to a Purchased state after checkout, and grants the exhibitor and all team members access on web and mobile via the aiNoteTakerEnabled flag.

stories.s: Sponsors and sponsored products can now be displayed in randomized order on the web platform, giving every paying sponsor fairer visibility rotation.
stories.pr: Sponsor and sponsored-product placement was fixed, so the same sponsors always appeared first, creating unequal exposure among paying sponsors.
stories.oc: A random sorting mode was added for Sponsors and Sponsored Products so their display order is shuffled rather than fixed by priority.

stories.s: Three-tier documentation for Native Integrations on the new Abstract Integration Schema was produced, equipping developers, managers, and clients to operate post-migration integrations.
stories.pr: The migration to the Abstract Integration Schema lacked structured documentation, leaving developers, support managers, and clients without a reliable reference for how native integrations work.
stories.oc: Developer, manager, and client-level documentation was created covering architecture and data flows, business capabilities, and client-facing configuration and troubleshooting.

stories.s: Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings are now managed from a single centralised admin location, simplifying how organizers configure meeting formats.
stories.pr: Configuration for the different meeting formats was fragmented across separate places, making organizer setup slow and inconsistent.
stories.oc: A centralised management area in the admin panel now controls Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings together.

stories.s: Organizers gained centralised admin-panel control over email templates for Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings, removing the need for scattered template edits.
stories.pr: Email templates for these meeting formats could not be managed in one place, forcing organizers to handle communications inconsistently across formats.
stories.oc: Admin-panel email-template management was added for Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings.

stories.s: Email-template management was extended to Exhibitor Events and Round Tables meeting formats, letting organizers self-serve communications for these formats from the admin panel.
stories.pr: Exhibitor Events and Round Tables had no dedicated email-template management, leaving organizers unable to control communications for these meeting formats.
stories.oc: Admin-panel email-template management now covers Exhibitor Events and Round Tables in Meeting Formats.

stories.s: Organizer tooling for managing Exhibitor Events within Meeting Formats was enhanced, giving organizers richer control over how exhibitor events are configured.
stories.pr: Existing Exhibitor Events management in Meeting Formats was limited, constraining how organizers could set up and run exhibitor events.
stories.oc: Enhancements were delivered to the Exhibitor Events management workflow in Meeting Formats for organizers.

stories.s: Round Tables can now be managed independently in the admin panel, decoupling them from other meeting formats for clearer organizer control.
stories.pr: Round Tables could not be managed on their own, coupling their configuration to other meeting formats and limiting organizer flexibility.
stories.oc: The admin panel now supports independent management of Round Tables as a distinct meeting format.

stories.s: Organizers can now control Lead Capture access by exhibitor category, enabling tiered lead-capture entitlements tied to sponsorship or category packages.
stories.pr: Lead Capture access could not be scoped by exhibitor category, so organizers could not differentiate the feature across exhibitor tiers.
stories.oc: Admin controls were added to grant or restrict Lead Capture access per exhibitor category.

stories.s: Lead Capture access can now be controlled at the individual exhibitor level, giving organizers fine-grained entitlement management beyond category defaults.
stories.pr: Lead Capture access could only be managed broadly, with no way to enable or disable it for a specific exhibitor.
stories.oc: Granular per-exhibitor controls for Lead Capture access were added to the admin interface.

stories.s: Product QR Code availability can now be gated by exhibitor category, letting organizers tie QR-code lead tooling to category-based packages.
stories.pr: Product QR Codes could not be controlled by exhibitor category, preventing organizers from differentiating this feature across exhibitor tiers.
stories.oc: Admin controls were added to enable or restrict Product QR Codes per exhibitor category.

stories.s: Product QR Codes can now be controlled at the individual exhibitor level, giving organizers precise entitlement control over QR-code lead tooling.
stories.pr: Product QR Code access could not be set for a specific exhibitor, limiting organizers to coarse, non-targeted control.
stories.oc: Granular per-exhibitor controls for Product QR Codes were added to the admin interface.

stories.s: Lead Capture Pro settings were consolidated into a single coherent configuration area, simplifying how organizers manage the premium lead-capture product.
stories.pr: Lead Capture Pro settings were scattered, making the premium product hard for organizers to configure and reason about.
stories.oc: Lead Capture Pro settings were unified into a consolidated settings experience in the admin interface.

stories.s: Module management for Meeting Format was restructured in the admin panel, providing a cleaner foundation for how organizers configure meeting-format modules.
stories.pr: The existing module-management structure for Meeting Format was unwieldy, making organizer configuration harder and constraining future extension.
stories.oc: The admin-panel module-management experience for Meeting Format was reorganised into a clearer structure.

stories.s: Attendee profile pictures now sync back to the GES/Visit integration with EP as the source of truth, keeping partner systems visually consistent with the EP platform.
stories.pr: Profile pictures held on EP were not pushed back to the Visit/GES system, and there was no reliable way to identify which visitors originated from Visit, risking sync errors and inconsistent profile imagery.
stories.oc: A profile-picture push-back capability was implemented for the GES/Visit integration, with profile pictures excluded from update mappings to prevent infinite update loops.

stories.s: Business Matching filters in the new recommendation service were reviewed and test-covered, ensuring the matchmaking engine produces accurate recommendations.
stories.pr: Business Matching filters had not been tested in the rebuilt recommendation service, creating uncertainty about whether recommendations were being filtered correctly.
stories.oc: BM filter behaviour was reviewed and understood, automated tests were added for each filter, and issues were either fixed or captured as linked follow-up tasks.

stories.s: The mobile app now supports matchmaking-based and randomized sorting of sponsors and sponsored products, aligning mobile sponsor visibility with the new web admin controls.
stories.pr: The mobile app only supported fixed set-priority sorting for sponsors and sponsored products, so it could not honour the new matchmaking and random sorting modes organizers configure on the web.
stories.oc: Mobile now reads the active sorting mode from the API and renders sponsors and sponsored products By matchmaking (score order) or Random (in-app shuffle, re-shuffled on each screen re-entry), while preserving existing set-priority behaviour and display limits.

stories.s: Search autocomplete now prioritises name matches over description matches, so attendees see the most relevant entity at the top of suggestion results.
stories.pr: In the IMEX search prototype, autocomplete sometimes ranked a description match above an exact name match, returning the wrong top result and undermining search trust.
stories.oc: Autocomplete ranking was changed so name matches are prioritised over description matches across and within entity types.

stories.s: Website Builder now lets organizers hide the call-to-action button on individual cards via a per-card toggle, removing the previous reliance on custom CSS.
stories.pr: Organizers could not hide the button on individual cards in the card component, forcing them to use custom CSS to control which cards showed a call-to-action.
stories.oc: A per-card toggle was added to the Website Builder card component so organizers can show or hide the button on each card independently.

stories.s: Closed a styling-consistency gap in Website Builder so every static card view can carry borders and shadows, giving organizers a uniform, professional event-site look without design hacks.
stories.pr: Some Website Builder static card views exposed border/shadow styling while others did not, producing visual inconsistency across the same page and forcing organizers into spacing/background workarounds.
stories.oc: Border and shadow options were added to the card views that previously lacked them, while views that already supported the styling were left unchanged.

stories.s: Tuned the AI search prototype ahead of the IMEX demo so 'did you mean' suggestions, gibberish handling and result counts behaved correctly, protecting a high-visibility client showcase.
stories.pr: The pre-demo AI search prototype mis-fired: suggestions showed on every result, gibberish still returned hits, and the result count did not match what was displayed.
stories.oc: Suggestion logic, no-match handling and result-count display were corrected for the demo build.

stories.s: The mobile app now enforces per-profile entitlements for Lead Capture and AI Meeting Notes, gating recording permissions per team member.
stories.pr: Mobile only knew a single global AI Note Taker toggle and had no per-category or per-profile control, so the platform could not enforce the new granular, purchasable Lead Capture Pro entitlements on the app.
stories.oc: The app reads backend per-profile flags to enable Lead Capture and AI Meeting Notes independently for each exhibitor owner and team member, with build-time gating of the recording module and mic/phone permissions and runtime gating via aiNoteTakerEnabled.

stories.s: Extended Meeting Program participation conditions to optionally cover exhibitor team members, giving sponsors and exhibitor teams more control over who can be met.
stories.pr: Participation conditions could not be optionally extended to team members, limiting how exhibitor/sponsor teams configured meeting eligibility.
stories.oc: Meeting Program now lets participation conditions optionally apply to team members (details specified in the linked spec).

stories.s: The Speed Networking algorithm now rejects invalid input with an error instead of silently ignoring it, preventing meetings in blocked slots.
stories.pr: On bad input (e.g. malformed blocked-timeslot boundaries) the algorithm silently ignored the data and only logged a warning, allowing meetings in blocked slots and masking integration defects - observed in logs after Hyve Shoptalk.
stories.oc: The algorithm now returns a 400 and logs an error for any input failing validation, applied broadly beyond just blocked timeslots.

stories.s: Built the sessions/agenda knowledge tool for the Phase-1 AI assistant so attendees can ask about sessions by day, topic, time or format instead of scrolling the full agenda.
stories.pr: Attendees had to manually browse the entire agenda to find relevant sessions; the AI assistant had no structured way to answer session queries.
stories.oc: A sessions tool was built and integrated into the AI agent, answering session questions by day, topic, time and format from structured event data.

stories.s: Refined how sponsored-meeting limits are validated on the Data Science side so admin/concierge-created meetings are not wrongly blocked, while genuinely new meetings are still checked.
stories.pr: Admins/concierges creating meetings during Meeting Program setup could exceed sponsored limits, and the existing validation did not correctly distinguish previously generated meetings from new ones.
stories.oc: Validation now skips previously generated meetings, checks only newly generated ones, and does not re-check post-generation.

stories.s: Added an API-toggleable rule that pools likes across an exhibitor's team members so an inactive teammate no longer drags down the team's matchmaking reach.
stories.pr: Matchmaking quality suffered when some exhibitor team members were inactive, because likes were treated per-member rather than shared across the team.
stories.oc: Likes are now de-duplicated and propagated across all team members of an exhibitor (grouped by Exhibitor ID), switchable via an API parameter, with docs updated.

stories.s: Brought organizer Campaign email recommendation blocks up to the visitor-side standard with clear boundaries and full-width card layouts, so event emails look consistent and professional.
stories.pr: In Campaign email templates, recommendation blocks for Products/News/Exhibitors lacked clear containers and wasted horizontal space, looking inconsistent next to the full-width Sponsors block.
stories.oc: Each recommendation block now has a consistent boundary and its cards use the full block width across Exhibitors, Products, News and Sponsors, on desktop and mobile, with no change to recommendation logic.

stories.s: Delivered a personalized web Meeting Notes list so attendees and exhibitors can capture and revisit notes tied to their meetings, deepening engagement with the networking workflow.
stories.pr: Users lacked a personalized, consolidated view of meeting notes on web, making it harder to recall and act on networking interactions.
stories.oc: A personalized Meeting Notes list was delivered on web (details in the linked specification).

stories.s: Ran structured QA on the public API v2 setCategory endpoint, logging defects as individual bugs to raise the reliability of the integration surface used by partners.
stories.pr: The /api/v2/account/setCategory endpoint needed systematic quality assurance to surface defects before partners relied on it.
stories.oc: The endpoint was QA-tested with discrepancies captured as linked individual bug tickets.

stories.s: Migrated the floorplan getStands endpoint to the modern V3 API, event-scoped with hall and last-modified filters, advancing the public API toward a consistent, partner-friendly contract.
stories.pr: The legacy V2 getStands endpoint lacked the event-scoped path and filtering of the V3 contract, fragmenting the integration surface.
stories.oc: getStands is now available as GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/floorplan/stands with hall and last-modified-range filters and pagination.

stories.s: Migrated the floorplan getHalls endpoint to the V3 API, giving partners an event-scoped, paginated halls resource as part of the broader API modernization.
stories.pr: The V2 getHalls endpoint predated the V3 event-scoped, paginated contract, adding inconsistency to the integration surface.
stories.oc: Halls are now served via GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/floorplan/halls with pagination and standard error envelopes.

stories.s: Migrated the global regions reference endpoint to V3 with localisation and modified-since filtering, modernising shared reference data for partner integrations.
stories.pr: The V2 location/regions endpoint lacked the V3 conventions (localisation header, modified-since filters, standard pagination/sorting) used elsewhere in the new API.
stories.oc: Regions are now served via GET /api/v3/locations/regions with country filter, localisation (x-lang), sorting and modified-since filters.

stories.s: Migrated the global countries reference endpoint to V3 with localisation and sorting, continuing the standardisation of reference data on the modern API.
stories.pr: The V2 location/countries endpoint did not follow V3 conventions for localisation, sorting and pagination.
stories.oc: Countries are now served via GET /api/v3/locations/countries with localisation (x-lang), ISO codes, sorting and pagination.

stories.s: Migrated the global session-languages reference endpoint to V3, keeping it un-scoped as before while adopting standard sorting and pagination for partners.
stories.pr: The V2 sessions/getLanguages endpoint lacked V3 conventions for sorting, pagination and response envelopes.
stories.oc: Session languages are now served via GET /api/v3/sessions/languages (global) with sorting and pagination.

stories.s: Migrated the event session-tags endpoint to V3 with event scoping, localisation and modified-since filtering, extending the modern API to session metadata.
stories.pr: The V2 sessions/getTags endpoint predated the V3 event-scoped, localisable, filterable contract.
stories.oc: Session tags are now served via GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/tags with localisation (x-lang), modified-since filters and pagination.

stories.s: Migrated the event session-types endpoint to V3 with event scoping, localisation and modified-since filtering, part of the session-metadata API modernization.
stories.pr: The V2 sessions/getTypes endpoint did not follow the V3 event-scoped, localisable, filterable conventions.
stories.oc: Session types are now served via GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/types with localisation, modified-since filters and pagination.

stories.s: Migrated the event session-tracks endpoint to V3 with event scoping, localisation and modified-since filtering, completing more of the session-metadata V3 set.
stories.pr: The V2 sessions/getTracks endpoint lacked the V3 event-scoped, localisable, filterable contract.
stories.oc: Session tracks are now served via GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/tracks with localisation, modified-since filters and pagination.

stories.s: Introduced a net-new V3 endpoint to retrieve event products programmatically, expanding what partners can pull from the platform via the public API.
stories.pr: There was no public API way to retrieve event product data; no V2 equivalent existed, leaving a gap in the integration surface.
stories.oc: A new GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/products endpoint was delivered with exhibitor, status and updated-since filters, localisation and pagination.

stories.s: Fixed a kiosk registration bug that force-uppercased emails and corrupted Turkish characters, removing a go-live blocker for BeautyIstanbul 2026.
stories.pr: In kiosk mode the Onsite Registration page auto-uppercased email input; Turkish casing rules turned 'i' into a dotted capital, producing invalid emails, failed delivery and a live-event blocker.
stories.oc: The kiosk email field now preserves the exact characters typed, so emails captured onsite remain valid.

stories.s: Added a badge-scan-gated email visibility setting in the mobile app so attendee emails appear only after their badge is scanned, balancing privacy with lead capture at IMEX.
stories.pr: IMEX needed attendee email addresses hidden until a badge scan, but the app had no setting to reveal email only after scanning, risking privacy concerns or lost contact ability.
stories.oc: A new toggle 'Show Visitor email ONLY after badge scan' was added; when enabled with profile email hidden, email appears on a profile only after a successful badge scan.

stories.s: Added natural-order sorting and multi-select bulk delete to the internal floorplan, sharply cutting the manual effort organizers spend managing halls and stands for large events.
stories.pr: The floorplan backend offered no sorting and no multi-select/bulk delete for halls or stands, forcing organizers of large events (e.g. 27-hall Agritechnica) to scroll and delete items one by one - slow and error-prone.
stories.oc: Halls and stands can be returned in natural alphanumeric order and selected (including select-all) for bulk deletion.

stories.s: In progress: a visual Session Calendar with weekly/daily views, overlap handling, a live 'now' indicator, and mobile responsiveness.
stories.pr: Attendees lacked a visual calendar to plan sessions across a week or drill into a single day, making agenda planning and comparison difficult, especially on mobile.
stories.oc: In progress: a Calendar Component giving weekly/daily session views, cascade layout for overlaps, '+N more' chips, a live now-indicator and mobile-optimised browsing (currently In Progress, not yet released).

stories.s: Attendees can now search the Session Calendar by title or speaker with real-time filtering and browse the agenda even while logged out.
stories.pr: Attendees had to manually scan the whole calendar to find sessions, the most relevant ones could be buried in overflow, and logged-out visitors could not explore the agenda before committing to sign in.
stories.oc: Real-time session search by title or speaker, relevance-based prioritisation in the grid (bookmarked, then popular, then featured), and logged-out browsing with intent-preserving sign-in prompts.

stories.s: Clicking a session now opens a slide-out drawer with full details, letting attendees bookmark it to their schedule without leaving the calendar.
stories.pr: Attendees had to navigate away from the calendar to see session details and had no quick way to build a personal shortlist from the calendar, disrupting agenda planning.
stories.oc: A 440px session Side Drawer showing image, title, track, type, speakers and a live badge, with in-place add-to-schedule and bookmarking plus visual indicators in the calendar grid.

stories.s: Corrected a misleading basket error message about order/payment deadlines so exhibitors get accurate guidance, reducing confusion on a live client environment.
stories.pr: The basket error wrongly referenced an expired 'payment date' and asked users to 'pay', when the platform has no payment deadlines and the order could still be placed - misleading exhibitors.
stories.oc: The message was reworded to reference an order deadline ('The order deadline for this section is [Date]. Please finalize your order by then.').

stories.s: Global search now suggests queries as attendees type, helping them reach the right people, sessions and content faster.
stories.pr: Attendees typed blind into search with no guidance, making discovery slower and less successful.
stories.oc: The global search field returns live autocomplete query suggestions as users type.

stories.s: Introduced a net-new V3 endpoint to retrieve event sponsors with full profile, category and placement data, broadening the public API's coverage for partner integrations.
stories.pr: There was no V3 endpoint exposing sponsor data with profile, category and visibility/placement flags for programmatic retrieval.
stories.oc: A new GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sponsors endpoint was delivered returning sponsor profile, category and placement configuration with pagination.

stories.s: Quality-assurance coverage was completed for the public Open API v2 exhibitor getList endpoint, hardening a data interface that external integrators and partners rely on.
stories.pr: The /api/v2/exhibitor/getList endpoint lacked formal, logged QA coverage, leaving the risk that defects in a partner-facing data feed would surface in production with no systematic bug tracking.
stories.oc: The exhibitor getList endpoint was fully exercised against its contract, defects captured as discrete linked bugs, and the endpoint signed off as QA-complete.

stories.s: QA coverage was completed for the Open API v2 exhibitor deleteGlobally endpoint, validating a destructive operation in a partner-facing interface.
stories.pr: The /api/v2/exhibitor/deleteGlobally endpoint had no formal QA coverage; an untested global-delete operation carries elevated risk of data loss or inconsistent behaviour for integrators.
stories.oc: The deleteGlobally endpoint was tested against its expected behaviour, bugs logged as linked items, and the endpoint signed off as QA-complete.

stories.s: The Speed Networking matchmaking engine was tuned to distribute meetings more evenly across participants, improving fairness so more attendees receive a viable schedule.
stories.pr: Meeting allocation in Speed Networking skewed toward some participants while others received too few meetings, producing an uneven, lower-value networking experience.
stories.oc: Two internal sorting strategies were trialled against production data, results compared via CSV, and the better-performing approach was shipped to production to flatten meeting distribution.

stories.s: The data-ingestion logic powering the new AI Search system was wrapped into a callable API with per-entity indexing pipelines and authenticated re-index/update/delete operations.
stories.pr: Ingestion existed only as standalone scripts, so there was no programmatic, authenticated way to (re)index search data per event or per record, blocking a productionised search service.
stories.oc: A FastAPI ingestion API now exposes full-event re-index, single-record upsert, and delete across all five entity types (exhibitors, products, sessions, people, news), with authentication and downtime-free indexing via Qdrant upserts.

stories.s: The AI Search and Ingest services were containerised, dependency-pinned, and pushed to AWS ECR, making the new search stack deployable and reproducible.
stories.pr: Without clean, version-pinned Docker images in a registry, the Search and Ingest services could not be reliably deployed or scaled in AWS.
stories.oc: Dead dependencies were removed and versions pinned, Docker images for both Search API and Ingest service were built and pushed to AWS ECR, and both containers passed local end-to-end tests.

stories.s: The AI Search stack was deployed to AWS ECS behind a load balancer with health checks, auto-restart, and traffic- and queue-based auto-scaling, making search production-grade and resilient.
stories.pr: The search services had no production runtime: no load balancing, health checking, automatic recovery, or scaling, so they could not handle real event traffic reliably.
stories.oc: Search API, Ingest service, and pg-listener run on ECS; the Search API sits behind an ALB with /health checks, crashed containers auto-restart, the API auto-scales on traffic, and ingest workers auto-scale on SQS queue depth.

stories.s: Real-time data synchronisation was built for AI Search so that changes in the platform database propagate into the search index continuously via a queue-and-worker pipeline.
stories.pr: Search data could become stale because there was no mechanism to stream database changes into the index in near-real-time, risking outdated search results during live events.
stories.oc: DB triggers on all five entity tables push changes to an SQS queue with DLQ retry; a worker processes sync jobs and auto-scales on queue size, a scheduled full re-index runs via EventBridge, and a pre-event completeness check guards data readiness.

stories.s: All AWS infrastructure for the Global Search system was codified in Terraform, giving the search stack reproducible, version-controlled, drift-free environments.
stories.pr: Search infrastructure risked being configured manually in the AWS console, causing configuration drift and making environments hard to reproduce or tear down reliably.
stories.oc: VPC/networking, ECS services, ALB, SQS, and EventBridge for the search system are defined in Terraform with remote S3+DynamoDB state, so a clean apply provisions a working environment with zero unexpected drift.

stories.s: The AI Search service was made highly available across two AWS zones, load-tested, and costed, de-risking it for production launch.
stories.pr: Before launch the search service ran without multi-zone redundancy, had no validated capacity limits, and lacked a running-cost estimate, leaving availability and budget risks unquantified.
stories.oc: The Search API now runs across two AWS availability zones, load testing was completed with Locust, and a monthly cost estimate covering AWS, OpenAI, and Qdrant was produced.

stories.s: AI Search now has production-grade observability: timing logs, a CloudWatch dashboard, alarms, and health checks across all five collections.
stories.pr: AI Search lacked production-grade monitoring, so slow responses, errors or crashes could go undetected and there was no operational visibility into search traffic, latency or collection health.
stories.oc: Every search request is timed and logged to CloudWatch, an ops dashboard covers traffic, latency and errors, alarms fire on errors, slow responses and crashes, and the /health endpoint now checks all five collections.

stories.s: The Import Participants feature is being brought under full automated-test coverage with consolidated business, technical, and test documentation following the standard quality process.
stories.pr: Import Participants lacked consolidated documentation and traceable automated tests, leaving a critical admin data-import flow vulnerable to silent regressions and knowledge gaps.
stories.oc: Not Clearly Specified (story is still In Progress; the five-step process of BA/tech docs, BE/FE/E2E test plans, test implementation into CI/CD, and QA sign-off is underway but not yet complete).

stories.s: A new native integration was built to pull registration and attendee data from D2i's Engage API into ExpoPlatform using the standard hub-and-spoke pattern.
stories.pr: Customers using D2i as their registration system had no automated way to bring attendee data into ExpoPlatform, forcing manual transfer and treating D2i as a disconnected source of truth.
stories.oc: A native D2i integration now searches and paginates the Engage Registrations API, supports delta sync via lastModified, and ingests attendee data into ExpoPlatform with D2i as the source of truth.

stories.s: An Exhibitor Analytics dashboard page was delivered, giving organisers visibility into exhibitor counts, profile completion, logins, engagement, and profile performance over time.
stories.pr: Organisers lacked a consolidated, self-serve view of exhibitor adoption and engagement, having to assemble these metrics manually from raw exports.
stories.oc: An Exhibitor Analytics page now charts exhibitor count by tier over time, profile-completion status with KPI cards and drill-down, login tracking, and engagement/profile-performance metrics (PRD R2-R5, R15).

stories.s: An Attendee Analytics dashboard page was delivered, surfacing attendee counts, profile completion, and engagement trends for organisers.
stories.pr: Organisers had no consolidated view of attendee adoption and engagement and had to derive these figures manually from raw login and profile exports.
stories.oc: An Attendee Analytics page now shows attendee count and profile completion with KPI cards plus an engagement/login dual-line chart, correctly excluding exhibitor categories and team-member logins (PRD R6, R7).

stories.s: A Platform Performance dashboard was delivered covering logins, active users, favourites, page visits, and engagement across the whole platform.
stories.pr: Organisers lacked a single view of platform-wide activity (logins, active users, favourites, page traffic), making it hard to gauge overall event engagement.
stories.oc: A Platform Performance page now shows web/app login activity with KPI cards, active users over time, favourites analytics with drill-down, and multi-page visit trends (PRD R8-R11, R16).

stories.s: A Mobile App analytics dashboard was delivered, tracking downloads, logins, adoption, and in-app page visits across iOS and Android.
stories.pr: Organisers had no consolidated view of mobile app uptake (downloads, logins, adoption rate, in-app traffic), leaving app performance opaque.
stories.oc: A Mobile App page now shows iOS vs Android downloads over time, login/adoption KPI cards with defined exhibitor and attendee app-login metrics, and an app page-visits table (PRD R12).

stories.s: A Connections Deep Dive dashboard was delivered, giving organisers detailed meetings and messaging analytics for their event.
stories.pr: Organisers could not easily analyse networking outcomes (meeting volumes, confirmation/cancellation rates, messaging directionality) without manual export crunching.
stories.oc: A Connections Deep Dive page now charts meeting status over time with KPI cards and exhibitor volume bands, plus messaging analytics (one- vs bi-directional) with drill-down (PRD R13, R14).

stories.s: A Sessions Deep Dive dashboard was delivered, ranking top sessions and session types by engagement for organisers.
stories.pr: Organisers lacked a ready view of which sessions and session types drew the most engagement, relying on manual export analysis.
stories.oc: A Sessions Deep Dive page now shows a Top-20 sessions ranked table and Top-5 session types by engagement, with filtering, sorting, and drill-down to session detail (PRD R17).

stories.s: A Products Deep Dive dashboard was delivered (currently in testing) covering product categories, top products, and listing metrics for organisers.
stories.pr: Organisers had no consolidated view of product-listing performance (top categories, top products, listing coverage), requiring manual favourites-export analysis.
stories.oc: A Products Deep Dive page provides Top-20 categories and Top-20 products ranked tables plus product KPI cards with filtering and drill-down (PRD R18); the story is in testing.

stories.s: A Sponsorships Deep Dive dashboard was delivered (currently in testing), reporting sponsor performance by asset type for organisers.
stories.pr: Organisers could not easily report sponsor ROI by asset (splash, banner, brand page, links) and risked miscounting Gold exhibitors as sponsors when pulling raw exports.
stories.oc: A Sponsorships Deep Dive page provides a per-sponsor/asset performance table (views, clicks, CTR) and sponsor KPI cards, with logic to filter to confirmed sponsors only (PRD R21); the story is in testing.

stories.s: Organisers can now point a Session's Register button to an external registration or payment URL, letting third-party systems handle session signup and payment.
stories.pr: Sessions could only use the platform's built-in registration, so organisers who needed external registration or paid-session handling had no supported path.
stories.oc: Organisers can configure a per-session external registration URL with a custom button label and an external-link icon, redirecting attendees to a third-party registration/payment page during pre-event and live event.

stories.s: The new Event Reporting dashboards were embedded as a dedicated sub-section under the existing Analytics module in the organiser admin panel, delivering the UX/UI integration for multiple dashboards.
stories.pr: The new Embeddable.com-powered reporting dashboards had no home in the product; organisers needed them surfaced inside the existing admin navigation without disrupting current analytics pages.
stories.oc: Not Clearly Specified (story is in testing; the dashboards — including Attendee Analytics, Connections Deep Dive, Logins, and Session Duration — are being embedded as a new Analytics sub-section in the left navigation, with several dashboards still at POC/awaiting-data stage).

stories.s: The sponsor display limit in the legacy view was raised to 150, allowing events with many sponsors to show them all in the older interface.
stories.pr: The legacy view capped the number of sponsors that could be displayed, hiding sponsors at larger events and undercutting the value promised to those sponsors.
stories.oc: The legacy-view sponsor limit was increased to 150, so all sponsors at higher-volume events render correctly.

stories.s: Universal pagination memory was implemented for required lists in the admin panel, so the platform remembers an organiser's page position as they navigate.
stories.pr: Admin-panel lists reset pagination on navigation, forcing organisers to repeatedly page back to where they were and slowing repetitive admin work.
stories.oc: Required admin-panel lists now retain pagination state across navigation, giving consistent page-position memory for organisers.

stories.s: Google+ was removed as an option from the brand-creation social media links, cleaning up a defunct social network from exhibitor brand profiles.
stories.pr: The brand-creation form still offered Google+ as a social media link even though the service has been discontinued, presenting an obsolete, confusing option to exhibitors.
stories.oc: Google+ was removed from the social media link options in brand creation, leaving only relevant, active networks.

stories.s: A new public API v3 endpoint was delivered that returns the sponsor categories configured for an event, letting integrators resolve sponsor category IDs.
stories.pr: Integrators consuming the v3 Sponsors endpoint received sponsorCategoryId values with no API to resolve them into human-readable category names, leaving a gap in the public API.
stories.oc: A GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sponsor-categories endpoint now returns paginated sponsor categories (id and title) with bearer authentication, enabling integrators to map sponsor category IDs to names.

stories.s: Adds the user-facing entry point that lets organizers describe website CSS changes in natural language, the first step of the AI-assisted Website Builder.
stories.pr: Organizers had no guided way to request styling changes to their event website without manual CSS work or developer involvement.
stories.oc: A UI entry point where a user can express desired CSS changes, wiring the front end into the broader AI website-builder flow.

stories.s: The Website Builder can now serialize a block's live HTML, style IDs, and design tokens on demand, giving the AI full context to generate accurate CSS.
stories.pr: Without a structured snapshot of a block HTML and design tokens, the AI had no reliable context to generate accurate, correctly scoped CSS in the Website Builder.
stories.oc: On demand the builder serializes the block rendered HTML with its data-styleid attributes and metadata map plus design-system tokens into a PII-free, safely truncated payload for the AI.

stories.s: Builds a secure backend proxy so the AI Website Builder can call AI providers without exposing credentials to the browser.
stories.pr: AI requests from the website builder needed a trusted server-side path; calling AI services directly from the client would expose API keys and create a security risk.
stories.oc: A backend proxy that brokers AI requests for the website builder, keeping provider credentials and orchestration server-side.

stories.s: TAMs can now preview AI-generated CSS and apply it scoped only to the block they are editing, so on-brand styling changes never leak into or break the rest of the event website.
stories.pr: Applying custom CSS risked bleeding into global styles and breaking other blocks or the whole event site, and there was no safe preview step before committing AI-generated changes.
stories.oc: AI-generated CSS is shown for review, then applied scoped to the block data-styleid only and never to the global CUSTOM_CODE_CSS block, with oversize CSS rejected and all other blocks left untouched.

stories.s: Non-technical users can now restyle event-website blocks in plain English, with AI translating requests into on-brand CSS using design tokens.
stories.pr: Styling a block previously required CSS and technical knowledge, blocking non-technical users from making even simple visual tweaks without developer help.
stories.oc: The AI CSS generator interprets everyday-language prompts with no CSS terms needed, maps colours to design-system tokens such as var(--primary-color), and cleanly refuses structural HTML changes as out of Phase 1 scope.

stories.s: Organizers can now choose exactly which content categories carry over when cloning an event, eliminating up to two days of manual cleanup.
stories.pr: Event cloning force-copied sponsors, news, sessions, local categories and floor plan, which organizers and TAMs then had to delete by hand, a painful process that could take up to two days for large events.
stories.oc: The clone dialog now offers independent checkboxes per content category with a confirmation summary, so only selected data is copied and manual post-clone cleanup is removed.

stories.s: Ships the Public API v3 POST /products endpoint to create a global, event-independent product record, advancing the v3 API migration and the global-vs-event product architecture.
stories.pr: The legacy API coupled products to events, so there was no clean way for integrators to create a reusable product entity decoupled from a specific event.
stories.oc: A new POST /api/v3/products endpoint that creates a global product tied to an exhibitor, with input validation and a standardized response envelope, no event binding.

stories.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators update a product's global fields directly, separating global data from event-scoped data.
stories.pr: The Public API had no v3 endpoint to update global product fields, and the older model did not cleanly separate global from event-scoped product data, complicating partner integrations.
stories.oc: A PATCH /api/v3/products/{productId} endpoint that updates only global product fields with partial-update semantics, 404 and 422 validation, and a standard response envelope, rejecting event-scoped fields.

stories.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators delete a product globally in one call, cascading its removal across every event automatically.
stories.pr: The Public API had no clean v3 way to delete a product globally and cascade its removal across all events, forcing integrators to manage event-level relations piecemeal without a single authoritative operation.
stories.oc: A DELETE /api/v3/products/{productId} endpoint that hard-deletes the global product and cascades removal of all event-scoped bindings (categories, custom fields, sponsorship, status) with 404 validation and a standard response envelope.

stories.s: Updates how exhibitor lead contribution is calculated so that meeting appointments feed into the lead scoring exhibitors see.
stories.pr: Exhibitor lead-contribution logic did not properly account for meeting appointments, under-representing the value exhibitors derive from booked meetings.
stories.oc: Revised lead-contribution calculation that incorporates meeting appointments into exhibitor lead metrics.

stories.s: A new diagnostic tool lets TAMs and non-DS developers see why the recommender produced given results for a tenant, removing a DS bottleneck.
stories.pr: Investigating recommendation issues (e.g. why a user gets no recommendations) required manually pulling in the Data Science team to inspect config, category mappings, matching rules and scoring, creating a support bottleneck and slow resolution.
stories.oc: A configuration-trace endpoint/UI returning system version, category snapshot, strict-matching config and scoring internals for a tenant/account/target, surfacing misconfigurations that suppress recommendations.

stories.s: Standardizes pagination behavior across the Admin Panel so organizers get a consistent navigation experience between list screens.
stories.pr: Pagination behaved inconsistently across Admin Panel screens, creating a disjointed and confusing experience for organizers.
stories.oc: A standardized pagination pattern applied across Admin Panel listings.

stories.s: Ensures a paid Sponsor's organization name is always shown across Session cards, pages, modals, recommendations and round-table/exhibitor-event surfaces, even when no logo is uploaded.
stories.pr: When a sponsor had no logo, their organization name could be missing from session surfaces, so paid sponsors did not get consistent, visible credit within the event.
stories.oc: Sponsor organization name now always displays across all session-related surfaces, alongside the logo or a standardized placeholder when none exists.

stories.s: Surfaces the session/exhibitor-event Type label on detail cards so attendees see the same Type information shown in the program list view.
stories.pr: The Type label appeared in the program list view but not on session/exhibitor-event detail cards, forcing attendees back to the list to understand what each item was.
stories.oc: Detail cards for Sessions and Exhibitor Events now display the Type label, consistent across Web, iOS and Android.

stories.s: Adds the hosting Exhibitor's name to Exhibitor Event detail cards so attendees can identify the organizer without returning to the list view.
stories.pr: The exhibitor (organizer) name showed in the program list but not on the Exhibitor Event detail card, so attendees could not identify the host from the detail view.
stories.oc: Exhibitor Event detail cards now display the hosting Exhibitor name, matching the list view across Web, iOS and Android.

stories.s: Implements universal pagination memory so the Admin Panel remembers a user's page position across listings, building on the pagination standardization effort.
stories.pr: The Admin Panel did not remember pagination state, so organizers lost their place when navigating away and back, repeatedly re-paging through long lists.
stories.oc: Pagination position is now retained (remembered) across Admin Panel lists, reducing repeated paging.

stories.s: Adds configurable preprocessing to the matchmaking engine that expands one-sided likes into mutual likes for specified role directions, improving meeting/speed-networking schedule coverage.
stories.pr: Non-mutual likes were not leveraged by the matchmaking algorithm, limiting the number of viable meeting pairs the scheduler could generate.
stories.oc: An API-configurable preprocessing step that transforms one-sided likes into mutual-like pairs per role direction before scheduling.

stories.s: Adds a mechanism to generate additional mutual-like pairs between users who have no existing likes, increasing meeting schedule coverage where demand signals are sparse.
stories.pr: When users had few or no likes, the scheduler had little to work with, leaving timeslots empty and meeting coverage low.
stories.oc: A configurable pre/post-processing mechanism that generates additional mutual-like pairs (per-user caps or timeslot-based) while respecting existing restrictions.

stories.s: Backend tracking story for removing the legacy '/newfront' path segment from URLs as part of the New Front migration, cleaning up legacy routing and technical debt.
stories.pr: URLs still carried a legacy '/newfront' segment from the old front-end, a remnant of the New Front migration that complicates routing and reflects accumulated technical debt.
stories.oc: Backend analysis and tracking toward removing '/newfront' from routing/config while keeping existing pages and APIs working (acceptance criteria pending backend impact analysis).

stories.s: Rearranges the Admin Panel navigation by moving the Sponsorship section as part of the broader Admin Panel restructure.
stories.pr: Sponsorship management was not located where organizers expected within the Admin Panel, contributing to navigation friction in the panel restructure.
stories.oc: The Sponsorship section was relocated within the Admin Panel navigation per the restructure plan.

stories.s: Restores Google Analytics support on event websites with GA4 integration and validation, re-enabling web analytics for organizers and exhibitors.
stories.pr: Google Analytics was not functioning on the platform (neither Universal Analytics nor GA4), so organizers lost web analytics tracking on their event sites.
stories.oc: Re-enabled and validated GA4 integration on the website, restoring analytics tracking.

stories.s: Adds front-end format validation, placeholder and help text to the Google Analytics (GA4) ID field in the Admin Panel, while still allowing an empty value to disable tracking.
stories.pr: The Google Analytics ID field accepted unvalidated input, allowing malformed GA4 IDs that break analytics, with no guidance on the expected format or conflicts with custom GA scripts.
stories.oc: The GA ID input now validates the GA4 format (G-XXXXXXXXXX), shows placeholder and help text warning against duplicate GA injection, and permits an empty value to clear tracking.

stories.s: Builds the redesigned chatbot front end in the Admin Panel (ExpoAssistant) using the Untitled UI library, wired to Data Science endpoints, as the v1 UI for the platform's AI assistant.
