stories.oc: A "Default view" setting (List/Grid/Calendar) in Sessions Config controls the first-visit layout for the Sessions page; once an attendee manually toggles view, their choice persists locally, and Exhibitor Events included in Sessions inherit the same setting.

stories.s: A Data Science analysis of tools and approaches for AI Agenda Builder implementation, with no further detail documented on the ticket.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Radio button styling is centralized into the shared component library, following the same consolidation already done for Switches.
stories.pr: Three separate repositories each maintained their own copy of Radio styling, causing drift and duplicated maintenance effort.
stories.oc: Radio styles are centralized in `expo-react-components`, reused across repositories with default-prop overrides in admin-ui, and removed from the individual repos.

stories.s: A search term in a shared or global-search URL now correctly filters News, Participants and Sessions results, closing a known Global Search v2 gap.
stories.pr: Only the Marketplace page read the `q` URL parameter on load (and even there the search box appeared blank); News, Participants and Sessions ignored it entirely, so global-search "view all" links and any shared/bookmarked search URL silently lost the search term.
stories.oc: News, Participants and Sessions now read `q` from the URL on load and filter accordingly; the search input correctly displays the pre-applied term on all four pages; global-search "view all" links now carry the term through.

stories.s: The admin "Remove clone" action now actually reverses a failed event clone's images, database rows and ledger entries, instead of doing nothing.
stories.pr: The "Remove clone" admin action was a guarded stub; a generic event delete cannot properly reverse a failed clone's copied S3 images, database rows, and clone bookkeeping.
stories.oc: `ExhibitionsController::removeAction` now deletes the cloned S3 images and Images rows per the copy ledger, deletes the cloned event (cascading DB cleanup plus the few non-cascading tables), and removes the clone job/step/progress bookkeeping.

stories.s: An RFC defines the DS-to-Visitors API contract for AI Agenda Builder recommendations so both teams can build in parallel instead of blocking on each other.
stories.pr: Without an agreed interface, the Visitors team (owning UI/booking) and Data Science (owning recommendations) would each build against assumptions about the other's contract, risking rework and sequential blocking.
stories.oc: A draft RFC document defines the request contract (user, booked slots, time window) and response contract (ranked session/event recommendations) between DS and Visitors, lists open questions and stakeholders, and is set up for the standard review process.

stories.s: A tenant-by-tenant audit of category-data completeness gives a go/no-go signal on whether AI Agenda Builder's matching logic has enough signal to work.
stories.pr: AI Agenda Builder's matching logic relies on interest categories being set on both exhibitors/sessions and registered visitors, but no one had measured how complete that data actually is across live tenants.
stories.oc: A tenant-by-tenant completeness audit of category assignment on exhibitors/sessions and registered visitors, checking taxonomy consistency, delivered as a short summary with a go/no-go recommendation for AI Agenda Builder feasibility.

stories.s: The exhibitor lead-questions modal's styling is corrected to match the approved Figma design after shipping visually inconsistent.
stories.pr: `LeadCustomModal.tsx`'s implemented styling diverged significantly from the approved Figma design.
stories.oc: The modal's styling is updated to match the provided Figma reference.

stories.s: A global React.lazy test stub, ported from a proven next14 fix, eliminates flaky non-deterministic unit test failures in admin-ui.
stories.pr: 59 source files use `React.lazy` + `Suspense` without any global test handling, so wrapper tests querying synchronously can run before a lazy child mounts, causing the same test files to intermittently pass or fail run-to-run under parallel Vitest workers.
stories.oc: A global synchronous `React.lazy` stub in `setupTests.tsx` renders lazy children immediately, wrapper tests are migrated off `waitFor`/`findBy` workarounds, and the suite is verified stable across multiple consecutive runs.

stories.s: Mobile header search gains the categories selector desktop already has, and the panel now pushes content down instead of overlaying it, per Figma.
stories.pr: The mobile header search never received the `searchPages`/`currentLanguage` props, so its categories selector never rendered, unlike desktop; the open search panel also overlaid page content instead of the approved in-flow layout.
stories.oc: `searchPages` and `currentLanguage` are threaded through to the mobile search component so the categories selector renders per Figma; the search panel is changed from an overlay to an in-flow layout on both breakpoints.

stories.s: Spike scoping whether AI Agenda Builder could use session likes/dislikes for smarter recommendations, without touching the live category-based Recommender rollout.
stories.pr: The Recommender powering AI Agenda Builder matches purely on declared interest categories and ignores behavioural signals (a user liking, disliking or removing a suggested session), so it can't adapt to what a user actually does.
stories.oc: Analysis-only deliverable: an inventory of where interaction data lives today, a recommended ingestion path into DS datasets with trade-offs, 1-2 candidate scoring approaches with effort estimates, and an explicit recommendation on next steps (new epic vs backlog addition vs defer). No code shipped.

stories.s: New "Use New UI Registration" toggle lets organizers migrate each event from legacy to new registration on their own schedule, defaulting off to protect existing events.
stories.pr: The New UI Registration is a major change with no way for organizers to control when their event switches over, risking broken flows for clients not yet ready to move off the legacy registration experience.
stories.oc: A new "Use New UI Registration" toggle in Event Setup > General > Settings, defaulting OFF; frontend registration routing and admin menu visibility switch between legacy and new flows based on the toggle, with the setting change taking effect immediately.

stories.s: Fixes two exhibitor-events display bugs: an empty floor-plan-location label and an incorrect Event Overlap flag on on-demand sessions.
stories.pr: The exhibitor events UI showed an empty "floor plan location" placeholder and flagged an "Event Overlap" warning even for on-demand sessions where the concept doesn't apply.
stories.oc: The empty floor plan location label is removed, and the Event Overlap indicator no longer shows for on-demand sessions.

stories.s: Spike proposing a dual-write from the existing event pipeline into the new Data Protocol 2.0 Kinesis stream, to validate it with real traffic before frontend integration.
stories.pr: The new API Gateway to Kinesis to ClickHouse pipeline exists but has no real traffic flowing through it to validate before the frontend experiment begins.
stories.oc: A design note, recommendation and effort estimate for extending the existing WS-pipeline Lambda to also copy each event into the new pipeline's Kinesis stream, covering schema mapping, record tagging to avoid double-counting, error isolation, and a kill switch.

stories.s: Reviews degraded Exhibitor Marketplace API endpoints against the new SLO framework and produces an improvement summary for the worst-performing latency sub-group.
stories.pr: Several Exhibitor Marketplace API endpoints (Critical-tier, 99.9% availability target) are running below their SLO targets, with the G_1200 latency sub-group flagged as degraded.
stories.oc: Identified the degraded G_1200 API sub-group and its endpoint list within the Critical Exhibitor Marketplace component, and produced an analysis/summary of the problem for improvement planning (the underlying SLO page itself notes several figures still need 4xx/background-job noise filtered out before being treated as confirmed breaches).

stories.s: Rebuilds the shared Checkbox as a pure-CSS, SSR-safe theme control (mirroring Radio) to fix a glyph-clipping bug and end per-app checkbox styling duplication.
stories.pr: Checkbox styling was duplicated across repos, and the shared library's checkbox used a bespoke SVG-based wrapper whose glyphs clipped at certain widths and which was client-only, blocking use in portal-ui's server-rendered Next.js theme.
stories.oc: A new CSS-drawn MuiCheckbox theme override ships in expo-react-components (SSR-safe, no SVG, no clipping), the old bespoke Checkbox wrapper is removed, and two accent variants (primary/info) are exposed; cross-repo adoption in admin-ui/portal-ui is scoped as follow-up work.

stories.s: Fixes a Node 22.4+ regression where the built-in localStorage shadowed jsdom's, which had broken 10 unit tests and masked real regressions.
stories.pr: Node 22.4+ ships a built-in Web Storage API that shadows jsdom's localStorage, so 10 storage-related tests fail on any modern dev machine or CI runner, hiding genuine regressions behind a known-failure baseline.
stories.oc: setupTests.js now forces jsdom's Storage implementation onto globalThis after initialization, restoring a fully green test suite and removing the noisy ExperimentalWarning.

stories.s: Updates mobile login to read independent OTP toggles for Individual vs Company profiles so authentication stays correct once web ships the split settings.
stories.pr: Mobile apps only understood a single global OTP flag; once web/admin ships separate OTP toggles for Individual vs Company profiles, mobile logins would break or show the wrong authentication method.
stories.oc: Mobile app now reads two independent OTP flags, shows the OTP screen or username/password screen based on the profile type being authenticated (Attendee vs Exhibitor Company, with team members following the individual setting), and preserves current behavior for events still on the legacy single-toggle config.

stories.s: Dedupes duplicated exhibitor-events selector logic and swaps hand-rolled chips for the shared design-system chip components.
stories.pr: SponsorsAutocomplete and SelectItem duplicated nearly identical search/render logic, and both used custom hand-rolled chip markup instead of the shared design-system chip components.
stories.oc: Shared search/render logic extracted into one component/hook, with chips now rendered via the expo-react-components shared chip/tag components.

stories.s: Ships a bbpr CLI and Claude Code skill so the frontend team can review Bitbucket PRs (list, diff, comment, approve) without leaving Claude Code.
stories.pr: Claude Code only integrates natively with GitHub, but the frontend team runs on Bitbucket Cloud, so PR reviews had to be done manually in-browser; the official Atlassian Rovo path is blocked pending org-admin API-token setup.
stories.oc: A bbpr CLI wrapper over the Bitbucket Cloud REST API, a bitbucket-pr-review Claude Code skill, a Bash permission allowlist, and a Confluence team setup guide, enabling list/diff/comment/approve on PRs from Claude Code.

stories.s: Adds support for custom track colors, per a minimal ticket with no detailed description available.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; the description contains only a Confluence short-link (not resolvable from the provided data) and rough FE/BE/QA day estimates.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Ships a new inbound HubSpot integration (contacts/companies to visitors/exhibitors) with configurable event scoping, opening the platform to HubSpot-using organizers.
stories.pr: Organizers running HubSpot as their CRM had no automated way to bring HubSpot contacts/companies into an EP event, and HubSpot's account-wide (non-event-scoped) data model had no way to map onto EP's per-event structure.
stories.oc: A polled, delta-driven sync (Contacts to Visitors, Companies to Exhibitors) via the AutoUpdate engine, three configurable Event Scoping strategies (Association/List/Filter-based), full field mapping, identity matching, custom field/category mapping, and archival/deletion handling.

stories.s: Onboarding spike that brings a second developer up to speed on the Round Tables architecture ahead of three upcoming feature stories.
stories.pr: Only one developer understands the Round Tables/Tabletalk placement architecture, creating a bus-factor risk just as three new stories (unique topic assignment, waitlist on decline, custom-field grouping) are queued up.
stories.oc: A written architecture alignment (current design summary in the new developer's own words, proposed extension points for each of the three stories, and agreed risks/open questions), reviewed by the original developer.

stories.s: New Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators upload media files to a global product, completing the v3 product-media capability.
stories.pr: The new global-vs-event-scoped product architecture had deferred product media file uploads; no V3 endpoint existed matching the pattern already used for image and video uploads.
stories.oc: New POST /api/v3/products/{id}/media endpoint supporting up to 10 files per product, content-based format validation, a 5MB cap, PDF thumbnailing, and a standardized response envelope.

stories.s: New Public API v3 endpoint removes a product media file safely, only physically deleting it once no other owner still references it.
stories.pr: No V3 endpoint existed to remove a previously uploaded product media file, leaving the media CRUD pair (upload/EP-55533) incomplete.
stories.oc: New DELETE /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} endpoint unlinks a media file from a product; the underlying file/row is physically deleted only when no other owner (exhibitor, schedule, message, etc.) still references it.

stories.s: Onboarding spike bringing a new DS engineer up to speed on the Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline architecture before hardening and testing work begins.
stories.pr: The engineer has near-term action items on the new data collection pipeline (action-ID investigation, ClickHouse testing) but no working familiarity yet with its architecture or scope.
stories.oc: A written summary of the pipeline architecture in the engineer's own words, reviewed by senior team members, plus documented open questions before the follow-on tickets start.

stories.s: Adds an isScheduled flag to the session calendar API so the calendar UI can highlight sessions already in a user's personal agenda.
stories.pr: The calendar-view endpoint didn't expose whether a session was already in the user's personal agenda, so the frontend couldn't distinguish scheduled from unscheduled sessions in the calendar grid.
stories.oc: Every session item in the day/week sessionsCalendarView response now carries an isScheduled boolean (always false for guests), with no other change to the response contract.

stories.s: Fixes an N+1 query and a null-dereference bug in hosted-buyer agent name lookups that would hard-fatal once the platform moves to PHP 8.
stories.pr: Hosted-buyer agent display-name resolution issues one uncached database query per agent and reads the result without a null check; on today's PHP 7.4 this silently blanks the name, but on PHP 8.x it hard-fatals, which would break the hosted-buyer filter and several admin list pages for any event with an agent missing that attribute.
stories.oc: Implementation hints proposed (batch-loading agent attributes once instead of per-agent, and null-guarding the read using the safe pattern already present elsewhere in the same controller); final implementation left to the developer.

stories.s: Adds a full calendar view (1-day/3-day grid, overlap handling, filters, search) to the mobile Exhibitor Events screen, matching the Sessions calendar experience.
stories.pr: The standalone Exhibitor Events List screen on mobile only offered a flat list with filters; unlike Sessions, it had no time-grid/calendar way to browse the exhibitor events programme visually.
stories.oc: A full calendar view for Exhibitor Events on mobile: 1-day/3-day grid, week-glance strip, overlap handling with overflow bottom sheets, track quick-filters, in-calendar search, filters, a Today button, and a toggle back to List View, driven by a web-configured default-view setting.

stories.s: Adds a MultiStandLocation component so multi-stand exhibitors display readably, and merges Sponsors onto ExhibitorCard so sponsor listings show location, tags and products.
stories.pr: Exhibitors with multiple stands showed an unreadable, ellipsis-truncated location string, and Sponsors couldn't show location, tags or parent/child info at all because SponsorCard was a stripped-down copy of ExhibitorCard.
stories.oc: New MultiStandLocation component ships in expo-react-components; ExhibitorCard now builds its own location from exhibitor.halls; ISponsor is merged into IExhibitor so SponsorsPopup renders full ExhibitorCards; the old SponsorCard is deprecated but not deleted, pending consumer migration.

stories.s: EDA on historical like/favourite data to determine whether it's dense enough to build and evaluate a smarter, interaction-aware session recommender.
stories.pr: A prior research spike (EP-55244/Confluence research page) proposed candidate ways to fold user likes into Recommender scoring but left "how would we even evaluate this" as an open TODO, and a 2023 experiment found interaction data too sparse to learn from.
stories.oc: An EDA write-up covering historical interaction volume/density (an updated sparsity verdict versus the 2023 LightFM baseline), exposure-bias/impression-data findings, and a recommendation on offline vs. online evaluation strategy for the two remaining candidate approaches.

stories.s: Exhibitor Import and Global Database additions now automatically carry an exhibitor's existing brands into new events, resolving a client-raised (ANWR) requirement.
stories.pr: Brands are cross-event assets, but the Exhibitor-Brand relation only persisted through event cloning; importing an existing exhibitor into a new event (or adding one from the Global Database) left their brands behind, forcing re-entry each edition.
stories.oc: Exhibitor Import (both new-to-event and update cases) and "add from Global Database" now auto-attach an exhibitor's existing brands, and their product/category relations where matches exist, to the target event, with no template or UI change required.

stories.s: Adds a nested Region sub-filter under Country (web only) so visitors can narrow exhibitor/participant listings by region, not just by country.
stories.pr: The Country filter was flat, with no way to narrow results to a region within a country, even on events where Region is captured on the registration form.
stories.oc: A new optional (default-off) Regions sub-filter nested under Country across Exhibitors/Pavilions/Brands/Products and Delegates/Speakers/Buyers admin tabs; web-only, with mobile explicitly unaffected.

stories.s: Polishes Global Search's results page (persistent search field, clearer counts, equal-size News cards, relabeled sponsor blocks) based on direct IMEX customer feedback.
stories.pr: Users at IMEX flagged friction points in the newly released Global Search results page: a closable search field that could disappear, confusingly placed result counts, an oversized first News card, and unclear sponsored labels.
stories.oc: The search field is now permanently visible below the sponsored banner; result counts moved onto "Show all" buttons with a summed page-level total; News cards are now equal-sized in a single scroll row; "Sponsors" relabeled "Sponsored Exhibitors"/"Sponsored Products".

stories.s: Onboarding/research task building developer fluency in Ticketing and a proposed new architecture (PR #4510) ahead of a planned Ticketing refactor.
stories.pr: No production changes; the team needs a developer fluent in both how Ticketing currently works end-to-end (admin setup, purchase, upgrades) and the new architectural pattern proposed in PR #4510, before any refactor of the current monolith code can begin.
stories.oc: Developer understanding of Ticketing end-to-end and the new architecture pattern from PR #4510, plus a documented list of candidate refactor areas; no code changes.

stories.s: Fixes IconModal's padding, gaps and title typography to match the Figma design system exactly, removing per-consumer style patches across ~41 call sites.
stories.pr: IconModal's theme styling had drifted from the Figma spec (wrong title size/line-height, wrong close-button offset, inconsistent padding/gap composition, missing border, wrong default width), affecting roughly 41 call sites in admin-ui plus shared library consumers, each patched locally instead of fixed at the root.
stories.oc: Reworked slot styles (uniform 24px padding, single 32px gap, correct 18px/1.2 bold title, 8px radius plus border, 424px default width), full Storybook coverage of slot combinations, and removal of local sx/width workarounds in admin-ui.

stories.s: Closes a bypass where direct URL navigation let restricted users open the add/edit product form even when the UI correctly hid the button.
stories.pr: The "can add/edit a product" gating logic lived only in the Add button's UI state; navigating directly to /profile/products?add=true (or ?edit=<id>) bypassed every disabling condition (limit reached, disabled products, relogin member), letting restricted users open and submit the product form anyway.
stories.oc: Routing decisions now use the same single "can add/can edit" gate as the button; unauthorized direct navigation redirects to the product list instead of rendering the form, with backend enforcement also to be verified.

stories.s: Scoping spike estimating the effort, risks and infrastructure needed to migrate the Exhibitors search engine to AI Search.
stories.pr: Before implementing the switch to AI Search (EP-55996), the team lacks a clear technical picture of the effort, risks and infrastructure requirements involved.
stories.oc: A technical brief (target state, gap analysis, risks/open questions, phased plan with T-shirt estimates) published and linked to EP-55996.

stories.s: Extends Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments search to match Account ID, so client ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East can cross-check transactions against Stripe quickly.
stories.pr: Search on the Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages covered name/surname/email but explicitly excluded Account ID, so the client (ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East) couldn't quickly cross-reference a transaction against their Stripe account/customer reference without scrolling paginated results.
stories.oc: The existing search field/button on both pages now also matches (partial) Account ID / ID, with the same trigger, reset and empty-state behavior as the original name/email search.

stories.s: Fixes product upload endpoints so slow file I/O no longer blocks the DB transaction and concurrent uploads can no longer silently overwrite each other's result.
stories.pr: Product upload endpoints ran slow external file I/O (up to ~10s) inside a database transaction, holding pooled connections under load, and two concurrent uploads or an upload racing a delete/update on the same product could silently overwrite each other's result, leaving an orphaned file in storage forever.
stories.oc: Uploads now validate and store the file first with no open transaction, then link it in a short transaction with permission/limit checks re-run; failed links auto-clean the stored file; concurrent writes to the same product now queue via row locking instead of silently overwriting; ~30 new unit tests, API contract unchanged.

stories.s: Fixes a caching bug where cookie-dependent/signed-in pages were marked publicly cacheable, risking one visitor's personalized page being served to another.
stories.pr: Every route, including signed-in and cookie-dependent pages, returned Cache-Control: public with no Vary: Cookie, so a shared CDN could serve one user's cached response (e.g. a signup redirect decision) to a different visitor.
stories.oc: Routes split into anonymous (kept public/cacheable) vs personal (private, no-store) groups; Vary: Cookie added where relevant; audited that no public response carries Set-Cookie; a route/header matrix handed to DevOps.

stories.s: Addresses remaining Global Search backend code-review findings: constructor-based config, policy-layer access checks, and hardened error handling.
stories.pr: Global Search's backend carries deferred code-review findings: brittle setter-based configuration, a duplicated access-control rule sitting outside the policy layer, catch-all exception handling, and DS failures silently reported as flags instead of raised as exceptions.
stories.oc: Constructor-based configuration, access rule moved into a policy, hardened typing and exception handling, followed by a review/QA pass.

stories.s: Rebuilds Switch to use theme color variants (mirroring Radio/Checkbox), deleting the custom Switch component in favor of a themed MUI Switch.
stories.pr: Switch was a custom component that defined its primary color directly in root styles instead of via theme color variants, unlike the already-unified Radio and Checkbox.
stories.oc: Switch colors implemented via theme variants; the custom Switch component deleted; usages replaced with FormControlLabel plus MUI Switch and slotProps; Storybook updated. Cross-repo consumer migration is separate follow-up work.

stories.s: Rebuilds Tag, StatusTag, Track, FilterChip and Badge as one theme-integrated Chip family so any app can restyle them via the MUI theme, additive to existing components.
stories.pr: Tag and StatusTag were built with ad-hoc sx functions and a string-keyed style lookup, not wired into the MUI theme, so consuming apps could only override them via sx/className, not theme.components.
stories.oc: A new chips/ category with 5 theme-registered components (Tag, StatusTag, Track, FilterChip, Badge) ships additively, alongside the untouched originals; cross-repo migration in admin-ui/portal-ui is scoped as follow-up work.

stories.s: Adds force and dry-run flags to manual AutoUpdate sync triggers, unblocking HubSpot Push-Back and future push-back integrations.
stories.pr: Manual AutoUpdate sync triggers had no way to bypass change-suppression gates (to force mapping changes through) or preview what a run would do without writing, a capability HubSpot Push-Back and future integrations like Cvent need.
stories.oc: force and dryRun flags threaded from the manual trigger through SyncJob to per-entity queue payloads; force bypasses both push- and pull-side suppression gates; dryRun logs WOULD_PUSH/WOULD_SKIP verdicts with no writes on the push side (rejected on the pull side); scheduled runs are unaffected; metrics track dry-run outcomes separately.

stories.s: Adds Paid amount and Payment status columns, plus a paid-only filter, to the registrant custom report, ending manual cross-referencing against the separate Payments report.
stories.pr: Payment data and registrant form data lived in two disconnected report systems, joined only through a multi-hop Registration to Account to Event to Participant to Order to Payment chain, so organizers had no single accurate view of who had actually paid.
stories.oc: "Paid amount" and "Payment status" (friendly labels: Paid/Pending/Failed/Cancelled/No payment record) added as selectable Visitor custom-report columns, plus a "Paid only" filter; registrants with no linked order are shown, not silently dropped.

stories.s: Extracts Saved Search Queries logic from the controller into a proper service/repository layer, fixing a replica-lag eviction bug by construction.
stories.pr: SearchSuggestionsController inlined the same account/event scope, a 20-entry cap rule, ad-hoc request parsing and a copy-pasted access gate across three actions, making the cap rule untestable without HTTP and vulnerable to a read-replica-lag bug on cap eviction.
stories.oc: New SavedQueryService plus read/write repositories (write operations forced onto the master connection), a request validation object, a response resource, domain exceptions, a feature-toggle module gate, a README, and unit tests for the cap/eviction rule; the controller becomes thin delegates and the existing 13-test behavioural suite stays green.

stories.s: Stops mobile Schedule, Speaker Profile and Exhibitor Profile pages from showing empty image placeholders, matching the fix already applied to the Sessions list.
stories.pr: The global "Display Image Placeholders" setting forced a large empty placeholder on Schedule, Speaker Profile and Exhibitor Profile pages whenever no logo/image was uploaded, and unlike web there's no CSS workaround available on the mobile app.
stories.oc: Schedule (both sessions and exhibitor events), Speaker Profile (session logos) and Exhibitor Profile (exhibitor-event images) now show nothing rather than a placeholder when no image is uploaded; every other list governed by the setting is unaffected; mobile only.

stories.s: Moves the Cloning module onto the standard module bootstrap and turns on automated architecture-boundary checks, unblocking the rest of its modernization.
stories.pr: Cloning is the only src/ module still on the legacy bootstrap path that once took the whole application down when it shipped without src/ present, and with no boundary-check gate, architecture conformance rests entirely on manual review, which two independent review passes already proved unreliable.
stories.oc: CloningModuleProvider replaces the legacy DI.php registration; new deptrac layer blocks (in warning mode) enumerate architecture violations; a CI pipeline step runs deptrac; a provider-resolution test guards every registered service; a live clone still runs end to end.

stories.s: Fixes the Cloning module's inverted dependencies so its core logic can be unit tested without a database and can't be silently broken by internal renames.
stories.pr: Cloning's Application and Domain layers depend directly on Infrastructure (and even on each other in the wrong direction), so basic logic can't be tested without Postgres, a viewer-permission decision leaked into a Domain value object, and CLI workers reference internal classes directly.
stories.oc: Contract DTOs introduced so Domain stops importing Contract; Application now depends only on ports; use-case classes moved into Application without dragging Infrastructure along; a thin CLI presentation layer added; the internal service-locator pattern removed; the contract split into read vs command halves, with deptrac reporting zero Domain/Application violations at completion.

stories.s: Documents the SharedKernel/Platform architecture rules (previously only in config comments) and fixes stale namespace references, to prevent repeat incidents like EP-55938.
stories.pr: The rules for where cross-cutting code belongs (SharedKernel vs Platform vs a new module) live only inside deptrac config comments with no README, and this already caused a real incident (EP-55938) where shared Alerting code was wrongly placed as its own module and had to be relocated; three existing READMEs also teach a namespace (Modules\\SharedKernel) that doesn't exist.
stories.oc: New README.md files for src/SharedKernel and src/Platform explaining what belongs where and the "cross-cutting is never a new module" rule (citing EP-55938 as the worked example); stale namespace references fixed in three existing READMEs; the outside-import axis and rule-document location gaps documented.

stories.s: Fixes the admin chatbot's RAG endpoint to be configurable per environment at runtime, preventing production admin traffic from silently hitting the dev AI service.
stories.pr: The Expo Assistant chatbot's RAG endpoint was effectively hardcoded to the dev Generation Service at build time with no working per-environment override; different Docker setups either lost the chatbot entirely (EKS) or baked in the dev URL, so production risked silently sending real admin oauth tokens to a dev-tier service with no in-app signal.
stories.oc: generate-config.js now emits the RAG endpoint into runtime config.js, regenerated on container start with no SPA rebuild needed; DevOps injects the variable per environment; verified across all four resolution paths. The equivalent problem in the legacy monolith admin is explicitly out of scope, tracked separately.

stories.s: Onboarding and impact-assessment spike scoping how much of Hyve's Flexible Generation Settings the existing Speed Networking service already supports.
stories.pr: A newly assigned engineer needs working knowledge of the speed-networking-service codebase and matching algorithm before Flexible Generation Settings (HV-265) can be accurately scoped into implementation.
stories.oc: A requirement-by-requirement assessment of what's already supported, partially supported, or net-new work for Flexible Generation Settings.

stories.s: Flags that opted-out users' favourites stay permanently private while their views/downloads/scans reappear on re-opt-in, and asks product to choose one consistent privacy model.
stories.pr: Favourites are protected on the write side (the event is never emitted for opted-out users, so the data never exists), while views, downloads and scans are protected only on the read side (the data is written but masked at query time), so opting back in retroactively un-hides a user's entire opted-out interaction history except favourites, and the read-side mask depends on a consent dictionary that's ~48% incomplete.
stories.oc: Three concrete options laid out (permanent write-side private tracking for everything, keep read-side masking as the standard, or split by signal strength) with measured costs and trade-offs for each, so the product team can make and record a decision.

stories.s: Fixes the OpenAPI doc generator to report real failures instead of always exiting 0, after a swallowed error already caused a spec-drift bug to be misdiagnosed.
stories.pr: composer docs always exits 0 regardless of failure, because the dispatcher discards exec() exit codes and each of the five doc generators swallows its own exceptions, so a stale, never-regenerated OpenAPI spec is indistinguishable from a fresh one.
stories.oc: The dispatcher now uses passthru() and stops at the first non-zero exit; all five generators write failures to STDERR and exit(1); behavior verified against real success and failure cases.

stories.s: Mutation-tests the Cloning pipeline's stuck-task monitor on dev/alpha, then schedules it across all production environments.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Triages and fixes 7 long-failing frontend test suites (39 tests) and 23 type-check errors so CI can gate on a clean green/red signal again.
stories.pr: 7 pre-existing failing test suites (39 tests) predate a recent unrelated change and mask any new regression in those suites, forcing every review to be gated against a stale "known failures" baseline instead of a clean green/red check, plus 23 pre-existing type-check errors in 2 test files.
stories.oc: All 7 suites triaged (stale test vs. real defect) and fixed, 23 type-check errors eliminated, and the full suite is green (0 failed of 1599 tests).

stories.s: Replaces VISIT's uncontrollable webhook resync (which could flood the queue) with guarded, observable AutoUpdate polling and a configurable near-real-time sync interval.
stories.pr: VISIT sync was an opaque black box — resync deleted and recreated the webhook from scratch with no lock, no progress visibility and no history, so repeated manual resync clicks stacked concurrent replays that flooded the processing queue until the integration stopped responding.
stories.oc: VISIT visitor/exhibitor sync migrated to AutoUpdate's revision-based polling (guarded against overlapping runs, visible in sync history); webhooks removed entirely; a new configurable per-subscription polling interval (VISIT gets 1 minute vs. the 5-minute default) preserves VISIT's near-instant feel; profile-picture push-back migrated to its own AutoUpdate subscription.

stories.s: Enforces braces on every control statement via ESLint, closing the gap between the documented code convention and what CI actually checks.
stories.pr: The FRON code conventions require braces on every if/else/for/while, but the inherited ESLint config only requires braces for multi-line bodies, so ~30 braceless statements exist and every new one has to be caught manually — the classic place where adding a second statement silently changes control flow.
stories.oc: .eslintrc now sets curly: ["error", "all"]; ~30 existing braceless occurrences auto-fixed; test suite and type-check baseline confirmed unchanged.

stories.s: Renamed 18 inconsistently-named constants files and removed a dead re-export shim so engineers stop copying the wrong naming convention.
stories.pr: Two inconsistent naming spellings for constants files (72 vs 18) caused convention drift, and a redundant root re-export shim added unnecessary indirection.
stories.oc: 18 files renamed to the standard *.constants.ts spelling, ~106-132 import sites updated, the dead systemPages re-export shim removed with its 24 importers repointed, and one unused file deleted.

stories.s: Fixed a timing bug so meeting-program and speed-networking timelines update live at the true start instead of only at the next segment's end, plus hardened animation and accessibility.
stories.pr: Users viewing the meeting-program/speed-networking timeline before it started would not see it update (e.g. the "Requests" block) at the actual start time - only when the first segment ended or the page reloaded.
stories.oc: useTimeline now wakes exactly at the segment start, self-heals from index gaps/duplicates, re-arms for waits over 24h, and the progress-bar animation moved to performant CSS transitions; added accessibility roles and 23 tests across the component.

stories.s: Authored the cross-team RFC defining how the meeting-generation algorithm will support organizer-configurable pair priorities and per-run settings, unblocking the next two build phases.
stories.pr: The current meeting-generation algorithm has a rigid, implicit priority model (sponsored/free-from-sponsored/free) that doesn't match new requirements for organizer-configurable pair ordering and per-run eligibility rules; the design needed cross-team sign-off (DS, Hyve backend, Hyve frontend) before implementation could be scoped.
stories.oc: An RFC was authored and readied covering the organizer-ordered pair-queue/priority model, per-run eligibility toggles (relevance requirement, shared team relevance, ignore blocked timeslots), open questions (e.g. "prioritise role" scope, a default-value mismatch), and rollout sequencing; no implementation shipped, per the ticket's explicit scope.

stories.s: Fixed the root cause of recurring flaky CI test failures and updated the QA agent's own standards so it stops generating the same class of async-assertion bug.
stories.pr: Unit tests failed randomly across parallel CI shards, blocking merges and eroding trust in build results ("developers learn to ignore red builds") - a recurrence of two earlier tickets whose fixes addressed only one mechanism, not the general class of bug.
stories.oc: Fixed at root cause by asserting on the actually-awaited async content instead of using loader-disappearance as a proxy; added an explicit async-assertion rule to the QA agent's skill doc and a repeated-run determinism check to its workflow so future generated tests can't reintroduce the same flake class.

stories.s: Registered 8 out-of-convention Redux store domains into the shared barrel so all store selectors and actions are reachable through one consistent import path.
stories.pr: Eight newer Redux domains skipped the required barrel-export registration, so imports were split between a documented "public API" barrel and inconsistent deep imports, undermining the convention's reliability.
stories.oc: Added index.ts barrels for the 8 domains and registered them in the central store barrel, resolving symbol-name collisions, without a disruptive bulk rewrite of existing deep imports.

stories.s: Re-leveled 188 legacy test cases to the correct, cheapest test layer and repointed them to their real future homes ahead of retiring the teststone tool.
stories.pr: Test cases inherited from teststone were almost all mis-classified as expensive end-to-end tests rather than placed at the cheapest layer that actually verifies the behaviour, and pointed at frozen teststone branches that won't exist once teststone is archived.
stories.oc: All 188 test cases re-leveled per the "lowest sufficient level" rule with justifications recorded, repointed to their real implementation repos, stale/mismatched cases corrected, and coverage gaps made explicit rather than silently over-claimed.

stories.s: Catalogued all API endpoints used for Exhibitor CRUD to ground the upcoming Exhibitor CRUD module build.
stories.pr: Before building or refactoring exhibitor CRUD functionality, the team lacked a documented inventory of which endpoints perform create, read, update and delete on exhibitors.
stories.oc: A list of Exhibitor CRUD endpoints annotated by action type (Create/Read/Update/Delete) was produced.

stories.s: Audited data availability for all 22 planned ExpoIntelligence metrics so the exhibitor-insights dashboard can be scoped against what the platform can actually deliver.
stories.pr: The ExpoIntelligence exhibitor-insights dashboard was only ~30% requirements-ready; without confirming real data existed for each of the 22 planned metrics, engineering risked estimating and building against metrics the platform can't actually support.
stories.oc: A findings report classifying each of the 22 metrics as Have/Partial/Missing with rough effort signals, cross-checked against the DP2.0 Parity Matrix; no dashboards or queries were built, per the ticket's explicit scope.

stories.s: Removed a slow full-team prefetch that delayed opening Bulk Respond for large exhibitor teams, replacing it with an instant open and a simple post-apply data refresh.
stories.pr: Opening Bulk Respond on any exhibitor team with more than 60 pending meeting-relevance assignments triggered a multi-request sequential prefetch before the button was even clickable, solely to build a client-side patch that was never rendered.
stories.oc: Bulk Respond now opens instantly regardless of team size; after a successful bulk action, only the current grid page is refetched fresh from the backend and every other cached page is invalidated.

stories.s: Migrated the Media module's public contract from internal value objects to plain primitives, keeping it aligned with the platform's modular, extraction-ready architecture.
stories.pr: The Media module's Contract layer still used SharedKernel value objects (ImageId, MediaId, id collections) in its public signatures, contradicting the newly-adopted convention that Contract surfaces must stay primitive and dependency-free so modules can eventually be extracted independently.
stories.oc: Media module Contract signatures now use primitives (int, int[], ?int); VO translation moved into facade implementations; consuming code (mainly the Product module) updated accordingly.

stories.s: Rolled out the FBM app's Gabarito typography to all remaining Android screens (~1010 elements across 451 layouts) for one consistent look end to end.
stories.pr: Only the "My Account" and "Event Info" screens used the new Gabarito font; the remaining ~451 layouts (about 1010 text elements) were left on inconsistent default fonts, breaking the intended unified look end to end.
stories.oc: Gabarito Semibold/Light configured platform-wide for FBM in AppBuilder; ~252 components (AppCompatTextView, TextView, MaterialButton, chips, radio buttons, text inputs) migrated onto the dynamic-font path; verified with no truncation/overflow on a smoke-tested set of high-traffic screens.

stories.s: Replacing four layers of hardcoded, drift-prone banner-size constants with the backend's own size data to stop paid sponsor banners from being repeatedly cropped in production.
stories.pr: Sponsor banner sizing was governed by hand-maintained frontend constants that repeatedly drifted from the admin-panel upload sizes and design, causing paid sponsor images to be silently cropped in production - three real, customer-reported incidents in a short window, each a regression of the previous fix.
stories.oc: A plan to drive banner aspect ratios from the API's own per-breakpoint size object (already returned by the backend but never read by the frontend), removing the per-page exception maps, aligning skeleton and resolved rendering, and replacing a silent 16:9 crop fallback with a dev-time failure.

stories.s: Added a "Back to search results" path so attendees can return to their exact Global Search context instead of redoing the search after opening a result.
stories.pr: Attendees who clicked into a result (exhibitor, session, product, etc.) from Global Search had no way back to their prior search results or query, forcing them to redo the search from scratch.
stories.oc: A "Back to search results" path now appears on detail pages reached via Global Search (restoring the query), consistently across all result types, and is absent when the detail page was reached any other way.

stories.s: Closed three code-quality gaps in the registration Tickets step - a duplicated constant, an unguarded null-price crash risk, and missing test coverage - with no visible change for participants.
stories.pr: A sold-out status key was duplicated across two files with nothing keeping them in sync; a ticket price field was destructured without a null guard despite one side of the codebase treating it as nullable, risking a crash on free tickets; and the component bridging registration to the shared tickets block had no test pinning its behaviour.
stories.oc: A single shared constant for the sold-out status key; a settled nullability contract with a guarded render path and test coverage for the price field; and a new render test pinning TicketingBlock's behaviour (event-over logic, currency/tax, features, page sizing, add/remove handlers).

stories.s: Documented that scanning a badge overrides a team member's GDPR opt-out but doesn't unlock their exhibitor's profile or Meet button, and asked for a decision on whether it should.
stories.pr: Scanning a badge is meant to make that person visible and contactable even with networking consent off, but the exhibitor profile's eligibility gate (team member list, Meet button) independently checks the raw GDPR flag and ignores the scan, so nothing changes for the exhibitor after a scan.
stories.oc: The ticket documents the gap and both possible resolutions (scan should also unlock the exhibitor, or an explicit statement that scan only ever unlocks the individual); this is a decision/description ticket, with no fix confirmed shipped in the text.

stories.s: Backend cache revalidation now hits the frontend's real endpoint directly, removing a redirect hop and a risk of silent stale-cache failures.
stories.pr: The backend's front-cache revalidation still targeted a pre-basePath URL that only works today via a temporary compatibility redirect; once that redirect is removed, revalidation would silently 404 and the site would keep serving stale cached content with no clear error signal.
stories.oc: Backend now calls /nextapi/revalidate/all directly in one hop instead of via the deprecated /newfront/api/revalidate/all redirect, verified with a single-hop 200 response on both the event and external domains.

stories.s: Refactored integration services onto constructor dependency injection so they can actually be unit tested.
stories.pr: Integration services took raw data plus collaborators in the constructor and populated collaborators from that data on the fly, which made unit testing them difficult.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and short description - the specific services and scope of the DI conversion are not detailed in the source.

stories.s: Rebuilt sitemap.xml and robots.txt generation on the frontend to fix broken, unindexable URLs and missing French-language pages that a client's SEO agency had reported.
stories.pr: The live sitemap for a client site (wineparis.com) was largely broken - 51 of 52 URLs were invalid relative paths pointing at redirecting addresses, no French URLs appeared at all, and robots.txt's Disallow directive was invalid - so French content stayed unindexed by Google, the exact issue the client's SEO agency reported.
stories.oc: Frontend now generates absolute, redirect-free sitemap URLs per event language with reciprocal hreflang annotations, covering entity pages as well as site-builder pages, plus a corrected robots.txt with a valid User-agent line.

stories.s: Implemented a crawlable language switcher with hreflang tags as part of the Technical SEO improvements effort, per a linked spec not independently verifiable here.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and its Technical SEO improvements epic - the description is only a Confluence link that was not listed as fetchable source material for this analysis.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Relocated 232 unit tests into co-located module folders under a new independent test root, decoupling the new DDD monolith's tests from legacy tooling.
stories.pr: Unit tests for the new src/ module-monolith code lived in a separate universal/ test tree rather than co-located with their modules, coupling the new architecture's tests to legacy tooling and blurring module boundaries.
stories.oc: All 232 tests relocated into co-located Tests/Unit folders per module under a new thin src/codeception.yml root with a shared test-kit base class, while universal's own Codeception config and tests remain untouched and green.

stories.s: Added an explicit priority mechanism for integration-event listeners so execution order no longer depends on accidental module-registration order.
stories.pr: Listener execution order was implicitly determined by the order modules were registered (MODULE_PROVIDERS), coupling unrelated concerns and making it risky to reorder modules without unintentionally affecting listener ordering elsewhere.
stories.oc: An optional priority parameter added to listener registration, sorted at dispatch time with a stable sort preserving today's default order, with test coverage for both custom-priority and default ordering.

stories.s: Moved round-table waitlist-replacement eligibility computation from an error-prone backend field into the matchmaking service itself, using data it already receives.
stories.pr: The round-tables replace API required the backend to pre-compute and send a filtered list of eligible replacement candidates for every declined seat, meaning it had to reconstruct, for every applicant ever, whether they'd ended up seated - something the backend found hard to compute reliably.
stories.oc: The Data Science service now derives eligible candidates itself (applied accounts minus every account already invited to a seat, across all generations and prior replacements) from data /schedule/ already receives; the unassigned_candidates field is removed from the contract entirely.

stories.s: Investigated why ClickHouse was overloading the Dev PostgreSQL instance to find and address the root cause.
stories.pr: DevOps flagged that ClickHouse, acting as the main data loader from Dev PG, was consuming all of Dev PG's resources.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title - the description states the problem and references a screenshot, but no resolution or root cause is recorded in the source.

stories.s: Upgraded portal-ui's zod/react-hook-form validation stack to current major versions across 24 files and 88 forms, succeeding a previously abandoned migration attempt.
stories.pr: portal-ui was pinned to a maintenance-mode zod v3 with an outdated hookform resolver and react-hook-form version; a prior migration attempt (EP-43768) had targeted the wrong branch, migrated only 2 of 16 files, and was never reviewed.
stories.oc: zod, @hookform/resolvers and react-hook-form upgraded across 24 host files (88 useForm sites), fixing the ~6 new type errors caused by removed v3-only options, with a manual regression pass of every zodResolver form.

stories.s: Shipped a placeholder API stub covering all ~53 ExpoIntelligence dashboard fields so teams can build against a stable shape before real data is ready.
stories.pr: Building the ExpoIntelligence dashboard's five pages card-by-card required a stable API shape to develop against, but real data for most fields wasn't ready yet.
stories.oc: A stub API returning the full field set across all 5 dashboard pages, with unpopulated fields explicitly marked -1 and a modular per-card response structure, validated by QA ahead of real data landing.

stories.s: Delivered real, precisely-defined metrics (leads, meetings, profile views, peer benchmarking) for the ExpoIntelligence dashboard's "Celebrate your wins" page, replacing placeholder data.
stories.pr: Page 01 of the ExpoIntelligence dashboard was running on the Story 1 stub's placeholder values; several metrics (leads captured, meetings held, peer comparisons) needed precise, unambiguous business definitions before real data could be trusted.
stories.oc: Every metric on Page 01 (leads captured, meetings held, profile views, message reply rate, peer benchmarking, best single day, etc.) now returns a real, queryable value with no -1 placeholders remaining, reconciled so totals match across cards.

stories.s: Delivered real lead-quality scoring, conversion funnel, and follow-up metrics for the ExpoIntelligence "Your leads" dashboard page, dropping metrics the platform can't actually support.
stories.pr: Page 02 was running on stub placeholders; metrics like lead quality (hot/warm/cold), the contact funnel, and unactioned leads needed firm, unambiguous rules before they could be trusted, and several previously-proposed metrics (company size, ownership) turned out to have no reliable underlying data.
stories.oc: Real values now power leads-to-meetings conversion, hot/warm/cold lead scoring, the capture-to-meeting funnel, unactioned-lead detection, peer conversion comparison, and reply-time metrics; unsupported metrics were explicitly removed rather than left as placeholders.

stories.s: Delivered real buyer-intent and product-interest metrics for ExpoIntelligence's "Buyer intent & products" page, rebuilding search and demo-request widgets around data the platform actually captures.
stories.pr: Page 03 was running on stub placeholders, and some originally planned metrics (typed search terms, demo requests) turned out not to exist in the platform's data, requiring those widgets to be redefined around real signals (filter/category selections, favourites).
stories.oc: Real data now powers top filter/category selections (replacing unsupported "search terms"), session-topic interest, uncovered-category gap detection via Product Profiles, and per-product views/saves signals; "demo requests" was removed from the API and UI rather than left as a placeholder.

stories.s: Designed a payload-content search feature for the V3 Logs page (covering request/response body, not just metadata) plus a top-nav entry point opening it to clients as well as internal teams.
stories.pr: The V3 Logs page's filters only covered request metadata (event, date, method, endpoint, etc.); there was no way to search inside actual payload content, so investigating an API issue meant manually scanning JSON entries one by one, which doesn't scale.
stories.oc: A full design was produced for a multi-condition payload search (search-in / field / match / value, up to 5 conditions, 7-day window cap for cost control) running on existing CloudWatch Logs Insights with no storage changes, plus a top-nav entry point to the Logs page for both internal and client users; this ticket delivers the design, not the implementation.

stories.s: Removed the deprecated Accompanying Persons step from the new Registration Pipeline builder so organizers can't configure an unsupported legacy option.
stories.pr: Organizers building or editing a registration form pipeline in the new registration engine could still select and configure the legacy, deprecated Accompanying Persons step, which is not supported going forward.
stories.oc: The Accompanying Persons step is no longer displayed, selectable or configurable in the Admin Panel pipeline builder; existing or cloned templates auto-strip it; participants never see it rendered in the new-engine registration flow.

stories.s: Added click/impression tracking and a near-real-time report on Mobile App homepage elements so client Hyve can report sponsor and exhibitor engagement performance.
stories.pr: There was no tracking of user engagement (views/clicks) with interactive homepage elements in the Mobile App custom pages, so the organizer had no data to report sponsor/exhibitor performance.
stories.oc: Impression/click events (with user ID, asset, action type, timestamp, request ID) captured for the sponsor banner, story reels and experience cards, exposed as a near-real-time (5-minute) report via Admin Panel Data Import/Export, with retry and dedup via request ID.

stories.s: Enhanced the multi-day session calendar view as part of the Session Calendar View improvements initiative; details not documented beyond the ticket title.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and its Session Calendar View improvements epic - the description is only a Confluence short-link that was not listed as fetchable source material for this analysis.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Redesigned session cards in the calendar view with an overflow indicator, part of the Session Calendar View improvements initiative; details not documented beyond the title.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and its Session Calendar View improvements epic - the description is only a Confluence short-link that was not listed as fetchable source material for this analysis.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Deleted the host app's broken, unused Storybook setup (196+ dead story files, 15 stale dependencies) since the design system's own Storybook already covers component isolation.
stories.pr: The host app's Storybook could not even start (a broken dependency on a Next.js internal module Next 14 renamed), had not been meaningfully used in over a year (1 story added, 14 deleted in twelve months), and its fixtures were stale against current component shapes - reviving it would cost more than it's worth.
stories.oc: Deleted 196+34 dead story files and the Storybook config, removed 15 unused devDependencies, reduced the host's outstanding TypeScript error count by roughly 40, and migrated the two tests that depended on a Storybook package to the standard testing-library equivalent.

stories.s: Fixed an iOS bug where sessions and exhibitor events hidden at the type level incorrectly vanished from an attendee's own My Schedule, notifications, deep links and calendar export.
stories.pr: When a session or exhibitor event's type (not the item itself) was hidden from public listings, it also incorrectly disappeared from an attendee's own My Schedule and every related surface, even though the attendee had already added it to their schedule.
stories.oc: Type-hidden sessions and exhibitor events now correctly appear in My Schedule and all related surfaces on iOS (matching Android), while item-level visibility restrictions and general Program/search discovery hiding remain unchanged.

stories.s: Migrated the last 27 legacy Tag/StatusTag usages across four repos to the new chips design-system family and added a lint rule to block future regressions.
stories.pr: An earlier chip-family migration was additive and left the legacy tags/Tag and tags/StatusTag components in place; a full four-repo audit found 27 call sites still resolving to the legacy family, almost entirely inside the shared component library itself, invisible to type or lint checks because of a barrel export.
stories.oc: All 23 in-scope library files plus one admin-ui file and one portal-ui alpha-branch regression migrated to chips/Tag, chips/StatusTag and chips/Track, with styling regressions (font size, truncation, border-radius, cursor) compensated for; an ESLint rule now blocks any new legacy import.

stories.s: Added all-day session support to the calendar view as part of the Session Calendar View improvements initiative; details not documented beyond the title.
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and its Session Calendar View improvements epic - the description is only a Confluence short-link that was not listed as fetchable source material for this analysis.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

stories.s: Extended the sessions calendar API with a multi-day endpoint and a dedicated days-with-sessions lookup, backing the frontend's multi-day calendar redesign.
stories.pr: The calendar-view endpoint only accepted a single selected day, and the list of days containing sessions was only obtainable as a side effect of the sessions search endpoint rather than its own dedicated call.
stories.oc: A new dedicated endpoint for the list of days with sessions; sessionsCalendarView now accepts an array of days instead of a single day; a conditional compact sessions-by-IDs endpoint depending on whether speakers stay in the main response.

stories.s: Root-caused a low-severity bug where a favourite made right after opting into networking consent silently fails to appear in Interactions, due to stale cached consent state in the browser.
stories.pr: A user who turns on Networking Opt-in and then stars someone without refreshing the page has that favourite saved and notified correctly, but the corresponding Interactions dashboard entry for the target is silently never created, because the client still holds the pre-change (opted-out) consent value cached from a 5-minute-cached auth response.
stories.oc: Root cause fully characterized and reproduced with timestamped evidence (client-side isGdprAccepted gate stale until reload); the ticket documents this as an investigation write-up rather than confirming a shipped code fix.

stories.s: Delivered the Data Science half of a click/impression reporting pipeline for Mobile App homepage elements, split from the operational-team side (EP-56995), for client Hyve.
stories.pr: Same underlying gap as EP-56995 - no tracking existed for engagement with Mobile App homepage interactive elements (sponsor banner, story reels, experience cards), leaving the organizer with no data to report sponsor performance.
stories.oc: The Data Science-owned portion (data schema and pipeline for the report: date, timestamp, asset, user ID, action type, near-real-time delivery via Admin Panel export, dedup via request ID) of the joint report delivery split with EP-56995.

stories.s: Locked the unreleased New UI Registration toggle down to the internal newdemo environment after an audit found it was live-switchable for any client admin.
stories.pr: The New UI Registration toggle had been deployed to production and was switchable by any admin, even though the new registration flow wasn't fully tested or released as Beta; an audit found it had already been turned on for a couple of non-demo events, though no live customer was actually affected.
stories.oc: The toggle no longer works for any client event; it remains functional only on newdemo for continued development and testing; the non-demo events found with it ON were switched back to the legacy flow; underlying functionality preserved for a future re-enable.

stories.s: Assessed the health of iOS's dormant 99-test E2E suite to decide whether to revive or rewrite it as the verification gate for a planned automated bug-fix pipeline.
stories.pr: The iOS EPUITests suite (52 files, ~4,500 lines, 99 tests) had been dormant since November 2024, never run in CI, with unknown build and pass status - but it's intended to serve as the verification gate for a planned Sentry-bug-to-fix automation pipeline, so its real state needed to be known first.
stories.oc: A timeboxed (2-day) spike deliverable: a written report on build status, per-test pass/fail with failure-cause classification, fixture and account liveness, wall-clock run time, and a revive-vs-rewrite recommendation with effort estimates; no code changes.

stories.s: Fixed the web app manifest to cache for an hour like the site's icons, eliminating a needless full network round-trip on every single page navigation.
stories.pr: Next.js's built-in manifest route hard-codes a no-cache response header with no ETag, and because the manifest link is re-inserted into the page head on every App Router navigation, the browser re-fetched it in full on every page change, unlike the app's icons, which cache for an hour.
stories.oc: Replaced the Next.js file-convention manifest with a custom route handler serving the same manifest JSON with the same hour-long cache policy as the icons, verified to produce zero repeat network requests within the cache window.

stories.s: Scoped an email digest for users as part of the communication channels work (details held on a linked Confluence page).
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; the description links to a Confluence page and a rough estimate only.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed email digest, estimated at 24 to 29 days depending on whether it is company-based.

stories.s: Fixes a public API server crash on exhibitor/set so parent and child exhibitor create/update requests return valid responses.
stories.pr: The public API server returned an empty reply (cURL error 52) on every exhibitor/set POST, failing 3 parent/child exhibitor tests.
stories.oc: exhibitor/set is to return valid JSON and create or update exhibitor records so the 3 tests pass.

stories.s: Fixes public API crashes on meetings/export so it returns correct JSON and status codes, including 403 for unauthorised users.
stories.pr: meetings/export crashed with empty replies on most requests and returned 500 instead of 403 for unauthorised users, failing 6 tests.
stories.oc: meetings/export is to return valid JSON with correct status codes (403, 400, 200) so ExportCest passes.

stories.s: Adds a V3 endpoint that returns a single product by its global ID, with its per-event categories, custom fields and sponsorship across every event it is bound to.
stories.pr: There was no V3 endpoint giving the fully expanded, cross-event view of a product; event-scoped reads only showed one event's bindings.
stories.oc: GET /api/v3/products/{id} returns the global product object plus an events array (eventId, categories, customFields, isSponsored), resolved to the x-lang language.

stories.s: Makes queue-based exports finish reliably by tracking batches explicitly instead of waiting for an exact row count that may never be reached.
stories.pr: Exports only completed when the buffer row count exactly equalled the total, so one lost or failed batch left the export stuck in progress forever (the 'stuck at 92.97%' case).
stories.oc: init records the expected batch count, each batch marks completion idempotently, and finalize runs when all batches are done or failed, for all BaseExport exports.

stories.s: Applies missing and corrected system translations, chiefly German, across exhibitor profile, registration photo, product list and notification screens.
stories.pr: Several screens showed wrong or missing German system translations, including team-member limit messages with broken number placeholders and badly worded registration photo labels.
stories.oc: The listed EN/DE strings were decomposed into child tickets and corrected; the story is in testing.

stories.s: Builds a serverless exceptions handler (SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB) with Grafana boards for all exceptions and bug candidates, plus a dry-run ledger of the Jira tickets it would raise.
stories.pr: Monolith exceptions were not grouped or surfaced systematically, so there was no reliable way to tell which exceptions represent real bugs.
stories.oc: A spec sized from a 38-day sample of the live stream and a repo exist; the MVP delivers two Grafana boards and a dry-run ticket ledger, now in review.

stories.s: Bulk connection delete now also removes opted-out users' private favourites, so they can bulk-remove what they bulk-added.
stories.pr: Bulk add correctly stored opted-out users' favourites privately, but bulk delete only touched account_connections and returned not_found for those private rows.
stories.oc: Bulk delete is aligned with single-disconnect behaviour and removes the owner's private favourite rows; the fix is in testing.

stories.s: Moves the cloning module's decisions into its domain layer with legacy model access behind ports and adapters, making cloner bugs cheap to unit test.
stories.pr: Every functional defect in cloning lived in entity cloners reachable only through Postgres-backed tests, with four still open on alpha, and legacy models imported the module directly.
stories.oc: Cloning logic sits in Domain behind ports, so each cloner decision becomes a fast table-driven unit test; the stage is in review.

stories.s: Moves the Alert component's look into expo-react-components theme overrides instead of each app reimplementing it with inline styles.
stories.pr: Alert existed only as a custom per-app wrapper that restyled MUI's Alert with ad-hoc sx for colours, variants, icons and layout.
stories.oc: Severity colours, variants, icons and spacing are to live in theme overrides so apps use a standard Alert; the change is in review.

stories.s: Adds a per-field "Null if empty" control to Integration Hub mappings so empty source values can be kept from wiping existing data.
stories.pr: When a source API returned null for a populated field, sync overwrote valid data, as when Genesis World wiped exhibitor categories (EP-55214).
stories.oc: Each create and update mapping row is to get a checkbox: ticked writes null as today, unticked skips the write and keeps the value.

stories.s: Sorts filter items alphabetically for sessions and exhibitor events (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumably filter items were not listed alphabetically.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; rough estimates only (BE 6 days, FE 2, QA 4).

stories.s: Adds a location filter for sessions and exhibitor events on web (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and epic (New filters for Sessions and Exhibitor events).
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to let attendees filter sessions and exhibitor events by location.

stories.s: Adds click and impression tracking to sponsor banners, story reels and experience cards in HYVE's App Builder custom blocks.
stories.pr: Interactive elements placed via custom HTML in App Builder captured no engagement data, so organisers could not prove sponsored placement value.
stories.oc: Tracking and a report with date, timestamp, asset and user columns are being built for unique and total engagement.

stories.s: Adds required (important) custom category filters to a popup (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to prompt users to set required custom category filters in a popup.

stories.s: Puts real data behind the insights portal page "Your team's engagement", covering registration date, logins, dashboard hours, messages and leads per team member.
stories.pr: Page 04 showed stub placeholder values from Story 1.
stories.oc: Each card is wired to defined metrics, such as per-session logins and first-touch lead ownership; the story is in testing.

stories.s: Gives control over Global Search blocks, labels, order and availability (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
stories.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
stories.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; marked Done.

stories.s: The Session Calendar side drawer tab now shows the organiser's configured name for the Tracks filter, including translations, instead of a hardcoded "By Track".
stories.pr: The side drawer hardcoded "By Track" although organisers can rename Tracks (e.g. to Streams or Topics), as the rest of the platform respects.
stories.oc: The tab label reads the Display Filter name from the Admin Panel, with localised variants; ready for release.

stories.s: Adds a sync_ts cursor to the accountsInteractions and sponsorInteractions APIs so clients can pull increments by server sync time without losing data.
stories.pr: Incremental pulls filtered by action time could miss records synced later, causing data loss for integrations.
stories.oc: sync_ts is returned per record and sync_from/sync_to accepted in the same millisecond format with a half-open window; in testing.

stories.s: The mobile Session Calendar View grid starts at the first session's time slot and ends at the last, with no empty hours to scroll past.
stories.pr: The calendar grid rendered empty time slots above the first and below the last session.
stories.oc: The visible range is computed per day from the grid sessions, excluding all-day sessions, snapping to slot boundaries.

stories.s: Mobile Calendar View moves sessions of 6 hours or more into an ALL DAY banner with a fixed 44px "+N" button, freeing the grid for shorter sessions.
stories.pr: Long sessions competed with time-specific sessions in the grid and squeezed their column width.
stories.oc: Sessions of 6+ hours are promoted to a banner in 1- and 3-day modes, excluded from overlap calculation, and still openable.

stories.s: API V2 sessions/set now accepts filter_1 to filter_5, so integrations can set custom session filters, matched in the request language.
stories.pr: Integrations could not set custom session filters through sessions/set.
stories.oc: Filters are applied leniently with per-slot errors, cleared with an empty string, and matched in the request language; done.

stories.s: API V2 session read endpoints now return filter_1 to filter_5, so integrators can read back the custom filters they set.
stories.pr: sessions/get and sessions/getSession did not include custom filter values, so values set via sessions/set could not be retrieved.
stories.oc: Both endpoints return five filter fields in the request language, and delta queries pick up filter-only changes; done.

stories.s: Widens the SearchField page-id helpers to plain strings and makes isKnownSearchPage a type guard, matching the untyped template data they receive.
stories.pr: Website Builder templates can hold 23 page ids but the type covered 12, so valid ids could not be expressed and tests relied on double assertions.
stories.oc: The helper half shipped in EP-57242 across next14 branches; the story is ready for release.

stories.s: Exposes the new sync_ts value in AccountsInteractionsReport so the accountsInteractions API can page by processing time.
stories.pr: The report layer did not carry ClickHouse's sync_ts, so the incremental sync path could not use it.
stories.oc: The report schema and pipeline include sync_ts with existing time behaviour unchanged; in testing.

stories.s: Exposes the new sync_ts value in SponsorAccountsInteractionsReport so the sponsorInteractions API can page by processing time.
stories.pr: The sponsor report layer did not carry sync_ts, so incremental sync could not use it.
stories.oc: The report includes sync_ts with stable pages and unchanged time behaviour; in testing, with a duplicates question open.

stories.s: Cloning an event via "create from parent" now remaps session type "Visible to" and "Available to" category ids to the cloned event's categories.
stories.pr: The legacy copyType() path copied session type audience settings verbatim, pointing at the source event's categories.
stories.oc: copyType() remaps account and exhibitor category ids onto the target event; the main clone path already did; in testing.

stories.s: Makes portal-ui request sized WebP image variants instead of original uploads, cutting image traffic and CloudFront cost.
stories.pr: 64.6% of image traffic was unsized originals and no WebP was requested, with images at 811 GB a day and about 69 USD of the daily CloudFront bill.
stories.oc: The frontend requests sized WebP variants through the existing resize lambda; done.

stories.s: Catalogues every consumer of ClickHouse analytics data across dashboards, reports, exports, APIs and UI, with its data sources and business rules.
stories.pr: There was no inventory of what reads ClickHouse data or which business logic each consumer applies.
stories.oc: A single catalogue lists consumers with owner, data sources and logic notes, reviewed by Bartosz Malec and Kostiantyn Shein; done.

stories.s: Opted-out users can now favourite and unfavourite exhibitors, visitors and products in the mobile app, privately, as they already could on web.
stories.pr: The app did not render the favourite option for opted-out users, so the same user got different behaviour on web and mobile.
stories.oc: The favourite affordance shows for opted-out users on all three surfaces, stored privately so the other party is never identified; done.

stories.s: Fixes the root error boundary placement so a crash shows an error page instead of a HierarchyRequestError loop and a blank page.
stories.pr: The only app-wide error boundary sat above the locale root layout, so any error stripped the html element, failed to append the fallback and looped.
stories.oc: A correctly placed boundary (e.g. global-error) is to render a fallback without destroying the document; in progress.

stories.s: Stops the admin floorplan treating a hall with no stands as a failed request, ending an ongoing unhandled Sentry error.
stories.pr: An empty hall returned data: [] and the shape guard rejected arrays, raising "Failed to fetch stand list" (51 events, 16 users).
stories.oc: Empty payloads are handled as valid, removing the unhandled rejection; ready for release.

stories.s: SAML 2.0 settings now have their own page in the Integrations catalog instead of the shared legacy settings page.
stories.pr: SAML still pointed to /admin/general/settings while hub integrations had dedicated pages.
stories.oc: A page at /admin/integrations/saml on the hub template reuses existing storage with no data migration, and the catalog entry points to it; done.

stories.s: Speakers see their pending values and a notice when profile changes await organiser approval, instead of thinking their data was not saved.
stories.pr: With pre-moderation on, speaker profile changes went to approval silently, which looked like a failed save (EP-56625).
